Who We Are

Identity, Thesis and Motto

One library. A world to enter. A community to build. Inward is forwards. Crypto first. Story second. Extraction never.

Who we are

EROS is a written body of work. It has cosmology, mythology, language, tokenomics, economic architecture, fiction, community philosophy, and immersive-world concepts. It has a website. It has a book library. It has a community that has, over time, produced a substantial archive of messages, video files, audio recordings, voice notes, animations, and stickers — much of it still sitting in Telegram, waiting to be catalogued and used.

EROS is also a proposed economic instrument, with an on-chain token, a set of deployed mechanisms, a set of designed mechanisms, and a set of proposed future mechanisms. The instrument is real enough to be inspected. It is not real enough to be promised. Every technical claim about it in any EROS production must be classified before it is spoken aloud.

EROS is also a community. It has a Telegram archive. It has contributors. It has people who have read the books, people who have not, people who own the token, people who are curious about it, people who want to help build something, and people who want to watch what happens next.

The EROS Series is the project of giving the books a life beyond the page. It is not a single television programme. It is not a single YouTube channel. It is not a single website. It is a connected media universe with several ways into it, and a community production system that lets the universe grow beyond what any central team could produce on its own.

The thesis

Inward is forwards.

This is the philosophical and visual organising principle of the entire project. It is not a slogan chosen for effect. It is the claim the books make: that the interesting direction of inquiry is not outward, into ever-larger structures, but inward, into the enclosure, the boundary, the relationship, the interior of the model, the thing that holds. The Cosmic Egg is an enclosure. The Torus has an inside. The Liquidity Tree has roots. The First Resonance has a room above a bakery. The instrument is a doorway, not the destination.

Every production in the EROS Series should be able to trace its central image or central scene back to this thesis. The cosmology episode is literal. The mythology episode is symbolic. The tokenomics episode is structural. The human story is emotional. But all four are, in their own register, about the inward direction.

The motto

Crypto first. Story second. Extraction never.

This is the order of operations, not the order of importance. The instrument comes first because it is the reason many people will find the project at all. The story comes second because it is the reason they will stay. "Extraction never" is the boundary: the project does not exist to extract value from its audience. It exists to build a world that people want to be part of, and to make participation real.

What we are making

We are making the EROS expression system: a way for the written library to become video, animation, documentary, comics, audio, interactive experiences, and community-created work, under a common identity, with common standards, and with a production pipeline that ordinary contributors can pick up and use.

The expression system has several layers:

  • The books. The 29-file source library. The canon. The thing everything else is downstream of.
  • The series. Fourteen shows, six cycles, one hub. The narrative architecture.
  • The media platforms. YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, audio, Telegram, the website. The distribution layer.
  • The Guild. Seven production studios. The community engine.
  • The website. The permanent home. The library that never disappears.

The expression system is not any one of these. It is the connection between them.

Why now

The books are written. That is the precondition. You cannot build an expression system for books that do not exist. The books exist. The website exists. The Telegram archive exists. The scripts for the first ten shows exist. The pilot treatments exist. The extraction database exists at version 0.3. The asset register exists at draft 0.1.

What does not exist is the operational document that lets a contributor open a page, understand the whole plan, find a task, complete it, and see it become part of the larger project. This document is that page. It is not the last page. It is the first page of the production era.

---

Part 1 · The Community Case

Why This Matters

Most tokens launch loud and go quiet. The founders take their fees, their inflation, their exit — and they walk. The tickers are still there. Nobody is home. Value extracts. The community is left holding a chart that no longer means anything.

EROS is built the other way round. The books are already written: cosmology, mythology, language, tokenomics, economic architecture, fiction, community philosophy, immersive-world concepts. The next task is not to write more. It is to give the existing library a life beyond the page — to turn it into a connected publishing, screen, digital-media and community-production system that the community itself can operate.

The central operating idea: one library, many doors, one creative Guild.

The core creative line: "If you do not own it, you're not in it."

The house motto: "Crypto first, story second, extraction never."

The core EROS thesis: "Inward is forwards."

The production system is ambitious in vision and deliberately simple in its first steps. We begin with work that can be made well using available people, tools and source material. Then we expand as capability and participation grow. We do not wait for a central studio. We do not wait for permission. We build the first complete example of the system, then make it easy for others to repeat.

The problem we are solving

A reader who picks up The Living Egg and reads it cover to cover knows what the EROS world model is. A person who has never heard of EROS and sees a twenty-minute video does not. The gap between those two states is the entire job of this project. The books are long. Many people will never read every volume. That is not a failure of the books. It is a fact about audiences.

The mission is to close that gap — to give people who will never read every volume a way in that respects the depth of the source without requiring its length. Through story, through animation, through demonstration, through the use of a visual metaphor that carries the concept. The expression system uses every tool available, not just the one the books already use.

The EROS answer

Build a universe people love because they built it. Not a universe handed down from a central studio. Not a universe that exists to extract value from its audience. A universe that people want to be part of, and that makes participation real. Ownership becomes participation, responsibility, contribution. The world is built by the people who show up to build it, and the people who show up are credited, respected, and able to see their work in the finished product.

The EROS phrase: "If you do not own it, you're not in it."

In this project, ownership also means participation, responsibility and contribution. It does not mean every contributor owns a share of the token. It means the world is built by the people who show up to build it, and the people who show up should be able to point at something and say "I made that."

TitanX on PulseChain — the army is already here

There are ten thousand TitanX holders who forgot they were given a uniform. The bear market took away the noise. It also gave time to build without anyone watching. The question is what happens when people start watching again.

The simplest, highest-leverage action is not creating another token or making enormous promises. It is reminding ten thousand holders what they already hold. The Front Door letter was addressed to the one person who did not walk away — Jake Sharpe built TitanX, and he knows who was here. The four-step sequence in that letter is the first public invitation of the EROS era. The people who stayed when there was nothing to extract are the signal, not the noise. Survival itself is the story.

Ten thousand wallets as a field of dark windows. One lights. Then ten. Then all of them. The price can open the door. Purpose is what makes someone stay.

The effect at scale — what this build-out actually produces

This is not a pitch. It is a slate. The scope is real, and it is measurable:

14

Shows

Numbered 00–13, across six cycles plus one hub. Scripts and storyboards exist for Shows 00–09. Treatments exist for Shows 10–13.

~4.5

Hours of finished picture

At 20 minutes per flagship episode across the slate, plus trailers, short clips, explainers and audio versions.

16

Anthology doors

Standalone shorts from Show 11, each a self-contained commission. The one format a decentralised studio can make in parallel.

10

Serial episodes

Show 10, The First Resonance, adapted as a ten-episode anime-influenced serial. Book Two becomes Season Two.

3

Thriller episodes

Show 12, The Continuity File, as a three-episode limited series. A slow thriller with a fiction contract and a real instrument.

12

Master shorts

Standalone vertical and horizontal shorts, each carrying one idea and one open loop. The discovery layer for every platform.

Plus the series trailer at 90, 30 and 15 seconds. Plus seven Guild studios. Plus an Open Call format that runs twice a week for six months. Plus a permanent website that holds every show page, every source book, every transcript, every diagram, every piece of evidence, every community contribution.

This is the largest transmedia build-out in the PulseChain ecosystem. Every finished piece increases demand for EROS and TitanX. Every burn increases scarcity. The universe is the engine.

The burn — how building the universe increases scarcity

EROS is a fixed-supply token on PulseChain. LIVE The supply is 333,333,333,333 — set at birth. The contract has no administrator who can rewrite the rules. Every transfer splits four ways:

🔥

Burn

Part is removed from circulation forever, toward the burn address 0x…0369. The burn address ticks only upward.

🪙

Staking

Part rewards stakers who hold and support the network over time.

🔒

Lock

Part locks staked tokens for a period, deepening commitment.

💧

Liquidity

Part deepens the liquidity pair, making the market more resilient.

Building the universe increases activity. Activity increases burns. Scarcity increases. The value stays in the hands of the people who built it. The design carries its strength and its consequence together. It operates without a discretionary admin, and that cuts both ways. No one can rewrite the rules, and no one can rescue a mistake. Renounced does not mean abandoned. It means the lever is gone. A coin built around a founder expires when the founder leaves. A network compounds.

The two vaults. LIVE One is steel and code — the on-chain vault: contract, rules, transactions, supply mechanics, liquidity arrangements, integrations. The other is a warm library — the cultural vault: books, mythology, art, education, videos, characters, websites, archives, creative assets. The flywheel is the connection between them. If people arrive only for a rising chart, they may leave when it turns red. If they find a universe they value, they have reasons to stay through the quiet seasons.

The flywheel — attention becomes participation becomes creation

Supply without attention dies. Attention without work leaves. Community without activity disappears. That is the autopsy report of most tickers that launched loud and went quiet. The flywheel is the answer. The cycle is a strategic hypothesis. Each transition needs to be built and demonstrated.

1 · Attention

A reason to look. Production and story bring attention. Market movement attracts newcomers.

2 · Discovery

A clear front door. A newcomer follows the front door into the books, mythology, tokenomics and the wider EROS universe.

3 · Understanding

The pieces connect. The viewer finds a concept they can now hold.

4 · Participation

A first useful action. The holder becomes a participant: reading, asking, testing, translating, drawing, writing, and building.

5 · Creation

New work and assets. Community contributions become new stories, artwork, assets, tools, and experiences.

6 · Renewed Attention

Useful work travels outward. The camera pulls back and reveals the archive has grown.

The narration line: "A token can attract a visitor. A story can hold their attention. But the real transformation begins when the visitor becomes a creator."

Production and story bring attention. Attention brings people in. The token and the web give them a stake. Participation funds more production. And the army may already be here. The price can open the door. Purpose is what makes someone stay. If people arrive only for a rising chart, they may leave when it turns red. If they find a universe they value, they have reasons to stay through the quiet seasons. The lock is the connection between the market cycle and the cultural cycle.

What this is not

This is not simply a television series. A television series is a single format, a single distribution channel, a single production pipeline. The EROS project is larger than that. It is a connected system that produces a television series as one of its outputs, alongside comics, audio, interactive fiction, tabletop scenarios, zines, short-form video, and community-created work.

We are not trying to turn every book into an episode. The 29-file library is not 29 episodes. It is a source register, and the 14-show slate draws from it selectively. Several books contribute to a single show. One book may support an entire serial. The mapping is by subject and theme, not by file.

We are not asking the community to invent EROS from scratch. The world already exists in the books. The community's job is to interpret, explain, illustrate, test, and build upon what is already there. The Guild provides the organised world. The community gives it living expression.

We are not claiming the EROS cosmology is established science. The EROS world model is a model. The books themselves make this distinction. The expression system must preserve it. The shows can be dramatic, cinematic, and awe-inspiring while being transparent about what is model, what is hypothesis, what is evidence, and what is fiction.

We are not claiming the token mechanisms are all live. Some are deployed. Some are designed. Some are proposed. Every production that discusses a mechanism must classify it before broadcast, and the classification must be checked against current on-chain data at the time of recording.

The EROS role: provide the architecture, standards, direction, initial examples and editorial coordination. We are not the sole producers. We are the team that holds the shape.

The Guild's role: bring the world to life. The Guild makes the diagrams, records the narration, draws the character sheets, animates the transitions, verifies the sources, builds the web components, edits the cutdowns. The Guild is the community production network, organised into seven studios, operating under contribution briefs, submitting work for review, and seeing accepted work enter the production canon.

A contributor in the Sound Studio can be more expert in their domain than anyone on the central team. The structure exists so that expertise can be applied without requiring every contributor to understand every other part of the project. The relationship between the two is not hierarchical in the sense of status. It is hierarchical in the sense of responsibility: EROS holds the standards and the final editorial decisions; the Guild holds the production.

Part 2 · How to Enter

The Four Doors

A person can arrive at EROS through any of several doors. They might arrive through a cryptocurrency question — they heard about the token, they looked it up, they found a video, they followed it back. They might arrive through an unusual cosmological idea. They might arrive through a story. They might arrive through a visual experience. They might arrive through a community invitation.

The job of the expression system is not to funnel everyone through a single entrance. It is to make every entrance a good entrance. Each one should give the visitor a reason to stop, something interesting to understand, something they can check, somewhere to go next, and something useful they can make if they choose to participate.

Four doors, not 29 file names. Four ways in, each one a good entrance.

Door 1 · Instrument

The Instrument

Understand the token, its architecture, and its economic mechanisms.

The main source material

The Newcomer Dossier, the Narrative, the Bridge, the Flywheel, the Liquidity Tree, the Platinum Standard, the Hopeful Future.

What this door holds

The token itself, its contract, its supply mechanics, its liquidity architecture, its relationship to TitanX and PulseChain, its flywheel thesis, its burn mechanism, its bridge, its bonding, its branching, its two vaults (on-chain and cultural), its Platinum Standard, its proposed future mechanisms, and its community-owned infrastructure thesis.

What a visitor should understand after entering this door

They should understand what EROS is as an instrument, what they actually own when they hold it, what is deployed and what is proposed, what the mechanism does when a transaction happens, what the liquidity tree is and how a token travels through it, what the Platinum Standard is and what role it is intended to play, and what the project's larger economic thesis is.

The tone of this door

Financial documentary, animated mechanisms, data visualisation, practical demonstration. The tone should be intelligent, mechanically satisfying, and honest about the difference between deployed, designed and proposed.

Mechanism badges used throughout

LIVE deployed and verifiable at the stated date. DESIGN an arrangement of existing components, no new contract. PROPOSED a future or undeployed mechanism. Any claim about contract ownership, total supply, transfer split, burn address, pools, liquidity or deployed token mechanics must be freshly verified before publication.

The shows in this door

SHOW 06 THE WEB Spot trades are hotel nights. Script & boards complete
SHOW 07 ROCK, RIVER, GATES Raise the price of gold and they mine more gold. Script & boards complete
SHORTS 06-A · 06-B · 06-C · 07-A · 07-B · 07-C Standalone cutdowns Six 45–60 second shorts, each an open loop. Scripted
Door 2 · World Model

The World Model

Explore the EROS cosmology, existence, and conceptual architecture.

The main source material

The Living Egg, the Eros Enclosure, the Conscious Eros, the Iteration Codex, the Garden of Eros, the 3D Universe.

What this door holds

The Cosmic Egg, the enclosure, the toroidal form, the two lobes, the crossover, the Isotope, the inner rind, the relationship between the interior and the observer, the proposed model of a universe that turns itself inside out, the concept of conscious EROS, the Iteration Codex's account of time, the Garden of Eros, the immersive 3D Universe, the proposed cosmological framework as a whole.

What a visitor should understand after entering this door

They should understand the EROS world model as a model — not as established science, but as a coherent, bold, internally consistent framework that proposes a different shape for the universe. They should understand the Cosmic Egg and the Torus as the two central visual images of that framework. They should understand the observer's place in the model. They should be able to distinguish between what the model proposes and what independent evidence supports.

The tone of this door

Cinematic CGI, narrated investigation, scientific comparisons, clearly labelled speculative models. The tone should be awe-inspiring without being credulous. The best model of this tone is a great science documentary that is willing to say "this is a model; here is what would have to be true for it to be correct."

Evidence labels used throughout

OBSERVED a measurement, record or event that can be independently checked. MODEL a conceptual or structural model stated by the books. HYPOTHESIS a proposed explanation that remains unproven. OBJECTION a substantive challenge. FALSIFIER a condition or observation that would weaken or disprove a claim.

The shows in this door

SHOW 01 INWARD IS FORWARDS A scientist deletes 85% of the matter in the universe and the math still works. Script & boards complete
SHOW 02 THE FOUR The only myth where the god walks away. Script & boards complete
SHOW 03 THE MOUTH Say SPREAD. Now say SPRAY. Script & boards complete
SHOW 04 LIFE FIRST Freeze a kilogram. Weigh it. Script & boards complete
Door 3 · Stories

The Stories

Experience the ideas through mythology, characters, and fiction.

The main source material

Gods of EROS, the Gift of Thoth, the First Resonance, Eros Stories, Men of Renown, the Continuity File.

What this door holds

The four operators —

Visual principle (from production pass): The four operators are recognised by what they do to the world, not by fixed character faces. Prefer function, geometry, light, hands, and bond over expensive character models — so the same grammar works in anime, documentary, CGI, comics, and live action.

NaUn, Ra-Shen, Thoth, EROS — as functions rather than characters. The language mystery of the Gift of Thoth. The mythic and speculative archive of Men of Renown. The First Resonance novel and its characters. The Continuity File. The Eros Stories and Sixteen Doors anthologies. The fiction contract that keeps fictional material clearly fictional.

What a visitor should understand after entering this door

They should understand who the operators are and how they function in the EROS mythology. They should understand the language framework the Gift of Thoth proposes. They should understand the human stories that bring the abstract framework down to scale. They should feel the emotional core of the project — the reason it matters to the people who are building it.

The tone of this door

Character animation, dramatic scenes, graphic myth, illustrated manuscripts, cinematic storytelling. The tone should be mythic and emotionally engaged, but it should not descend into a conventional pantheon of rival personalities. The operators are functions. The fiction is clearly fiction.

The two rails used throughout

Rail A — Documented History. Primary sources, statutes, public records, dates, citations, falsifiable claims. Show 08 and the Illumination Strategy.

Rail B — Mythic and Speculative Archive. Men of Renown, Masks, and the fictional material. It must carry an explicit fiction or speculation contract. The two rails may be compared at clearly identified structural points, but fictional events must never be presented as documented history.

The shows in this door

SHOW 08 FOOTPRINTS The sentence is real. The story is not. Script complete · research verification remains
SHOW 09 MASKS Two loud doors. One quiet one. Script & boards complete
SHOW 10 THE FIRST RESONANCE The number he did not type. Ep 1 script · Ep 2–10 beat sheets
SHOW 11 SIXTEEN DOORS Pick a door. Doors 1–3 scripted · 4–16 outstanding
SHOW 12 THE CONTINUITY FILE Which form covers this? Framework · key scenes · incomplete
Door 4 · Applications

The Applications

Discover how the library becomes a living community and production system.

The main source material

The Eros Plan, the Architecture of Participation, the Front Door, the Open Call, We Are With You, the Media index.

What this door holds

The plan itself. The production system. The participation architecture. The newcomer journey. The Guild. The Open Call format. The community invitation. The media index. The 3D Universe as a participatory space. The whole apparatus by which the community takes the books and makes things.

What a visitor should understand after entering this door

They should understand how to participate. They should understand what the Guild is, what the seven studios do, how to pick up a contribution brief, how work is reviewed, how credit is given. They should understand that the project is not a broadcast — it is an invitation. They should see that there is a place for them, whatever their skill.

The tone of this door

Real footage, interviews, tutorials, behind-the-scenes content, AI-assisted storytelling. The tone should be welcoming, practical, and honest about what has been done and what is still being built.

The contribution pathways used throughout

The single task. The personal project. The studio cell. The experimental branch. The research contribution. These are not mutually exclusive. A contributor can start with a single task, move to a personal project, form a studio cell, and eventually produce a branch. The system is designed to let contribution grow.

The shows in this door

SHOW 00 THE MAP Nobody hands you a shield. They hand you a chart. Script & boards complete
SHOW 13 THE OPEN CALL One paper. One camera. Episode 1 skeleton · weekly format
THE GUILD Seven studios · one task board Writers · Visual · Animation · Sound · Research · Web · Publishing Starter kit ready · first 10 tasks defined
THE INVITATION Build with us or fractally branch off The Empty Column is yours. Open

The public journey. Curiosity → Understanding → Investigation → Exploration → Participation → Creation. Each stage corresponds to a different kind of content. The journey is not linear. A person can arrive at Participation without going through Investigation. A person can arrive at Creation after a single piece of Curiosity. The stages are not gates. They are stations on a map, and the map should be visible from every station.

The five rules for making content at every stage. Give people a reason to stop. Give them something interesting to understand. Give them something they can check. Give them somewhere to go next. Give them something useful they can make.

The Applications

Purpose: Discover how the library becomes a living community and production system.

Main source material: Eros Plan, Architecture of Participation, Front Door, Open Call, We Are With You, Media.

What this door holds: The plan itself. The production system. The participation architecture. The newcomer journey. The Guild. The Open Call format. The community invitation. The media index. The 3D Universe as a participatory space. The whole apparatus by which the community takes the books and makes things.

What a visitor should understand after entering this door: They should understand how to participate. They should understand what the Guild is, what the seven studios do, how to pick up a contribution brief, how work is reviewed, how credit is given. They should understand that the project is not a broadcast — it is an invitation. They should see that there is a place for them, whatever their skill.

The tone of this door: Real footage, interviews, tutorials, behind-the-scenes content, AI-assisted storytelling. The tone should be welcoming, practical, and honest about what has been done and what is still being built.

The shows in this door: From Holding to Building (Show 05), The Open Call (Show 13), The Map (Show 00), and the community segments of every other show.

Part 3 · The Scope

The 14 Shows

Fourteen shows across six cycles, anchored by one interactive hub. This is the working production architecture — the most developed and coherent structure in the source documents. It supersedes earlier provisional episode counts as the current working slate. The earlier four-strand concept remains the public navigation system. The earlier 22-episode proposal remains a historical development plan and a source of ideas. It is not a competing production slate.

This is not a pitch. It is a slate. Scripts and storyboards exist for Shows 00–09. Treatments exist for 10–13. Six books are fully extracted into a production database. The remaining 23 are indexed and mapped. The first public release is five pieces: a trailer, The Map, Receipts, Inward Is Forwards, and The Open Call. Everything else follows if those land.

14 Shows
6 Cycles + 1 Hub
29 Source Files
6 Fully Extracted
10 Shows Scripted
16 Anthology Doors

The four doors are the public navigation system. The 14 shows are the narrative architecture. Each show maps to one of the four doors, and each show draws from a cluster of source books. The mapping is by subject and theme, not by file. Several books contribute to a single show. One book may support an entire serial.

Part 4 · The Plan

The Plan

The Plan is the spine. It is written to be read end to end by the coordinating team and to be entered by section by contributors. It is not a summary. It is not a pitch. It is the operating document.

How to use this document. Read the Mission and What We Are Making as the argument. Read the Audience Journey and the Source Library as the navigation. Read the Show Architecture as the slate. Read Production Grammar and Canon Rules as the standards. Read the Book-to-Media Engine and Guild as the operating system. Read the First Release and 90-Day Plan as the launch. Read the Appendices as the reference shelf.

Version 1.3 · 15 November 2026. This is the consolidated working source of truth. It preserves the decisions already made, records what is complete and incomplete, and gives the next working session a precise execution brief. Change rule: update this document when a real project decision changes, not every time an idea is discussed. Record the decision, date, reason and affected sections. Keep previous versions.

The Plan · §1

1. The Mission

The EROS books have been written. The immediate task is no longer to keep adding material indiscriminately. It is to give the existing body of work a clear path of expression.

We are building a system that can:

  • turn the source library into a connected public experience;
  • translate its strongest ideas into accessible, technically sound and engaging media;
  • provide a repeatable production method for long-form episodes and short-form discovery content;
  • give the EROS community a practical Creative Guild through which people can contribute;
  • keep the source material, editorial decisions, factual claims, scripts, assets and published outputs connected;
  • reduce friction so the community can begin producing useful work without waiting for a large studio or a perfect finished series.

Central operating idea: one library, many doors, one creative Guild.

Core creative line: "If you do not own it / You're not in it."

House motto: "Crypto first, story second, extraction never."

Core EROS thesis: "Inward is forwards."

The production system should be ambitious in vision and deliberately simple in its first steps. We should begin with work that can be made well using available people, tools and source material, then expand as capability and participation grow.

The books exist. The gap is expression.

EROS has a substantial body of written work. The first and most important fact is that the work is done: cosmology, mythology, language, tokenomics, economic architecture, fiction, community philosophy, immersive-world concepts. The books are written. They are not waiting to be written. They are waiting to be expressed.

The gap is not creative. The gap is translational. A reader who picks up The Living Egg and reads it cover to cover knows what the EROS world model is. A person who has never heard of EROS and sees a 20-minute video does not. The translation between those two states is the entire job of this project.

The mission is to close the gap between the people who already understand the books and the people who could understand them if the books were expressed in media they already use. That is the whole mission. Everything else — the 14 shows, the seven studios, the asset register, the evidence system — is a means to that end.

The seven objectives

The Master Project and Guild Blueprint names seven objectives. They are worth stating in full because they are the criteria against which every production decision should be measured.

  1. Make the books accessible to people who will never read every volume. The books are long. Many people will not read them. That is not a failure of the books. It is a fact about audiences. The expression system exists to give those people an entry point that respects the depth of the source while not requiring the length of it.
  2. Communicate difficult ideas through compelling stories, visuals, demonstrations and explanations. The ideas in the EROS library are dense. They can be explained in prose. They can also be explained through story, through animation, through demonstration, through the use of a visual metaphor that carries the concept. The expression system should use every tool available, not just the one the books already use.
  3. Give each book a natural place within a larger EROS universe. A book is not a standalone artefact. It is a contribution to a world. The expression system should show the relationships between books: this book expands that one; this book depends on that one; these two books are alternative treatments of the same idea; this book contradicts that one and here is the log of the contradiction. The universe is the connection, not the collection.
  4. Create a permanent, navigable online home for the material. The website is the home. It is not a marketing site. It is the library. It should be mobile-first, fast, searchable, easy to navigate. It should hold every show page, every source book, every transcript, every diagram, every piece of evidence, every community contribution. It should be the place that never disappears, even if a social platform does.
  5. Use modern distribution platforms to reach new audiences. YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, audio platforms, Telegram, X. These are the discovery layer. They are not the library. The library is the website. The platforms are the roads that lead to it.
  6. Give the EROS community a practical structure for making its own productions. The Guild is that structure. Seven studios. Contribution briefs. A submission process. A canon approval process. The community should not have to invent its own process every time it wants to make something. The Guild provides the process.
  7. Build a growing archive of work that can be reused, expanded and improved. Every production should make the next production easier. The asset library, the character bible, the visual grammar, the episode templates, the prompt library — all of it should accumulate. A contributor should not have to start from zero. They should be able to stand on what has already been built.

What we are not doing

We are not simply making a television series. A television series is a single format, a single distribution channel, a single production pipeline. The EROS project is larger than that. It is a connected system that produces a television series as one of its outputs, alongside comics, audio, interactive fiction, tabletop scenarios, zines, short-form video, and community-created work.

We are not trying to turn every book into an episode. The 29-file library is not 29 episodes. It is a source register, and the 14-show slate draws from it selectively. Several books contribute to a single show. One book may support an entire serial. The mapping is by subject and theme, not by file.

We are not asking the community to invent EROS from scratch. The world already exists in the books. The community's job is to interpret, explain, illustrate, test, and build upon what is already there. The Guild provides the organised world. The community gives it living expression.

We are not claiming the EROS cosmology is established science. The EROS world model is a model. The books themselves make this distinction. The expression system must preserve it. The shows can be dramatic, cinematic, and awe-inspiring while being transparent about what is model, what is hypothesis, what is evidence, and what is fiction.

We are not claiming the token mechanisms are all live. Some are deployed. Some are designed. Some are proposed. Every production that discusses a mechanism must classify it before broadcast, and the classification must be checked against current on-chain data at the time of recording.

Our role and the Guild's role

Our role is to provide the architecture, the standards, the direction, the initial examples, and the editorial coordination. We are not the sole producers. We are the team that holds the shape.

The Guild's role is to bring the world to life. The Guild makes the diagrams, records the narration, draws the character sheets, animates the transitions, verifies the sources, builds the web components, edits the cutdowns. The Guild is the community production network, organised into seven studios, operating under contribution briefs, submitting work for review, and seeing accepted work enter the production canon.

The relationship between the two is not hierarchical in the sense of status. It is hierarchical in the sense of responsibility: we hold the standards and the final editorial decisions; the Guild holds the production. A contributor in the Sound Studio can be more expert in their domain than anyone on the central team. The structure exists so that expertise can be applied without requiring every contributor to understand every other part of the project.

The Plan · §2

2. What We Are Making

This is not simply a television series. It is a connected EROS media and learning ecosystem, with a television-style editorial spine.

The ecosystem has five mutually supporting parts:

1. The source library

The books, HTML pages, diagrams, arguments, stories and technical material already created. The canon. The thing everything else is downstream of.

2. The editorial and canon system

The method for deciding what a source says, what it means, how it connects to other sources, and how it may responsibly be adapted.

3. The show and publishing slate

The structured sequence of episodes, serial fiction, explainers, investigations and community formats. Fourteen shows, six cycles, one hub.

4. The distribution system

A permanent website/library, YouTube as the principal video home, short-form platforms for discovery, audio/podcast distribution, and Telegram/community channels for participation.

5. The Creative Guild

The community production network that turns clear briefs into scripts, research, artwork, animation, sound, web experiences, translations and published work. Seven studios, one task board, clear credit.

The website is the permanent home and index. YouTube is the principal screen destination. Short-form media introduces people to individual ideas and directs them to the deeper work. The Guild creates the work and helps it circulate.

The expression system

We are making the EROS expression system: a way for the written library to become video, animation, documentary, comics, audio, interactive experiences, and community-created work, under a common identity, with common standards, and with a production pipeline that ordinary contributors can pick up and use.

The expression system has several layers:

  • The books. The 29-file source library. The canon. The thing everything else is downstream of.
  • The series. Fourteen shows, six cycles, one hub. The narrative architecture.
  • The media platforms. YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, audio, Telegram, the website. The distribution layer.
  • The Guild. Seven production studios. The community engine.
  • The website. The permanent home. The library that never disappears.

The expression system is not any one of these. It is the connection between them.

Why now. The books are written. That is the precondition. You cannot build an expression system for books that do not exist. The books exist. The website exists. The Telegram archive exists. The scripts for the first ten shows exist. The pilot treatments exist. The extraction database exists at version 0.3. The asset register exists at draft 0.1.

What does not exist is the operational document that lets a contributor open a page, understand the whole plan, find a task, complete it, and see it become part of the larger project. This document is that page. It is not the last page. It is the first page of the production era.

The seven-layer mission in one sentence

Give each book a natural place within a larger EROS universe, create a permanent navigable online home for the material, use modern distribution platforms to reach new audiences, give the EROS community a practical structure for making its own productions, and build a growing archive of work that can be reused, expanded and improved — so that every production makes the next production easier.

The Plan · §3

3. Audience Journey & Public-Facing Structure

Do not make newcomers understand the whole EROS universe before they can enter it. Give them a small number of clear doors.

A person can arrive at EROS through any of several doors. They might arrive through a cryptocurrency question — they heard about the token, they looked it up, they found a video, they followed it back. They might arrive through an unusual cosmological idea — they are interested in models of the universe, they found the Living Egg, they started reading. They might arrive through a story — they read the First Resonance, they wanted more. They might arrive through a visual experience — they saw the 3D Universe, they wanted to explore. They might arrive through a community invitation — someone they know said "come help build this."

The job of the expression system is not to funnel everyone through a single entrance. It is to make every entrance a good entrance. Each one should give the visitor a reason to stop, something interesting to understand, something they can check, somewhere to go next, and something useful they can make if they choose to participate.

The four public doors

Instrument

What EROS is as a token/instrument, how it works, and what is documented about its design and operation.

World Model

The EROS cosmology, philosophical framework, operators and models, with clear labels distinguishing model from established science.

Stories

Mythology, fictional narratives, characters, worlds and speculative archives.

Applications

Participation, community, architecture, tools, liquidity concepts and practical projects.

A visitor should be able to start with one question or one short piece and then follow a clear path into a longer episode, source text or practical participation opportunity.

The public journey

The desired audience path is:

Notice →

Served by short-form video, by striking images, by the opening of an episode, by the hook. It asks nothing of the viewer except attention.

Understand →

Served by the flagship episodes, by the explainers, by the illustrated articles. It rewards the viewer with a concept they can now hold.

Explore →

Served by the website, by the library, by the 3D Universe, by the connections between shows. It rewards the viewer who wants to go deeper.

Verify →

Served by the source references, by the evidence labels, by the transcripts, by the primary documents. It rewards the viewer who wants to check.

Participate →

Served by the community, by the Telegram, by the Open Call, by the contribution briefs. It rewards the viewer who wants to do something.

Create →

Served by the Guild, by the studios, by the accepted work and its credit. It rewards the contributor who wants to make something that lasts.

Share

The final stage. Useful work travels outward. The viewer becomes a distributor. The flywheel turns.

The journey is not linear. A person can arrive at Participation without going through Verification. A person can arrive at Creation after a single piece of Curiosity. The stages are not gates. They are stations on a map, and the map should be visible from every station.

The five rules for making content at every stage.

  1. Give people a reason to stop. The first two seconds of a short, the first thirty seconds of an episode, the first paragraph of a page. If the opening does not earn attention, nothing after it matters.
  2. Give them something interesting to understand. The content must teach something. Not a summary of the book, not a list of facts, but a concept the viewer can take away and use.
  3. Give them something they can check. The content must reference its sources. The viewer must be able to follow the trail back to the book, the page, the claim. This is not optional. This is how the project earns trust.
  4. Give them somewhere to go next. Every piece of content should end with a door. The next episode, the related book, the website page, the community discussion. The journey is the point.
  5. Give them something useful they can make. The content should invite participation. Not every viewer will accept, but every viewer should be shown the invitation.

Every published item should make the next step obvious

Avoid forcing every visitor through a long introductory lecture. The public journey is the design principle. Every piece of content is a station on the map, and every station points to the next one. The Map is the entry point. It explains how the cycles connect and lets a viewer choose a direction. The cold-viewer sequence is: Trailer → Show 00: The Map → Show 05: Receipts → viewer choice of world.

Ownership

The EROS phrase is: If you do not own it, you're not in it.

In this project, ownership also means participation, responsibility, and contribution. It does not mean that every contributor owns a share of the token. It means that the world is built by the people who show up to build it, and that the people who show up should be credited, respected, and able to see their work in the finished product.

Ownership is also a design principle for the production system. A contributor should be able to point at something and say "I made that." A contributor should be able to see their name in the credits. A contributor should be able to reuse the assets they and others have made. The system should be built so that contribution is visible, cumulative, and credited.

The Plan · §4

4. The 29-File Source Library

The original EROS ZIP contains 29 HTML files. They form the foundational source library. They are not all the same kind of document. Some are books. Some are technical guides. Some are stories. Some are navigation and community documents. Some are immersive-world materials. The production system must preserve those differences.

⚠ Extraction status — the honest number.

6 of 29 sources are fully extracted and verified. The extraction workbook reached version 0.3 with 165 passages across six core texts. The remaining 23 sources are indexed and mapped, but their detailed passages, scenes, claims and visual instructions have not yet been extracted into the working database.

An earlier document (EROS_Master_Series_BibleR.md) describes all 29 files as fully extracted using a 12-field register. The Unified Master Television & Series Bible v1.0 and the Master Project v1.1 both state that only six core texts have been fully extracted. Do not silently choose one statement. The production rule is: treat the six-book extraction as verified, treat the 29-book extraction as claimed-but-unverified, and complete the audit before any script rewrites that depend on the extraction.

The six verified sources: The Living Egg, The Eros Enclosure, Gods of EROS, The Flywheel, Architecture of Participation, The First Resonance. Together: 165 sections, approximately 86,152 words.

4.3 The six fully extracted books

The extraction workbook (version 0.3) records that six books have received a full structural extraction:

4.4 The 23 outstanding books

The remaining 23 files require the planned extraction pass. This is not a gap in the source library — the books exist. It is a gap in the production pipeline: the 23 files have been indexed and their destinations mapped, but their detailed passages, scenes, claims and visual instructions have not yet been extracted into the working database.

The 23 outstanding files are all files except SRC-001, SRC-010, SRC-012, SRC-019, SRC-020, and SRC-021.

4.5 The extraction discrepancy

There is an important discrepancy in the source record. The Master Series Bible R describes all 29 files as having undergone a rigorous 12-field extraction. The Unified Bible (v1.0) states that only six core texts have been fully extracted.

The PDFs state that the 12-field structure is valuable, but the earlier register should be audited against the actual source passages before its entries are treated as verified. The production rule is: do not spend time rewriting existing scripts until this audit has been done.

This is not a problem to be papered over. It is a problem to be logged, reconciled, and resolved. Until it is, the production system should treat the six-book extraction as verified and the 29-book extraction as claimed-but-unverified.

Required source extraction fields. For every source, capture at least: source ID and canonical filename; exact title and source version/date if present; source purpose and intended audience; section/chapter/heading structure; core thesis and supporting arguments; important definitions and canonical terminology; exact passages worth quoting or adapting with section/page/anchor references; claims that require verification; models, hypotheses and speculative interpretations; fictional/story elements and character material; mechanisms and their status (LIVE, DESIGN or PROPOSED); diagrams, symbols, visual metaphors and animation opportunities; examples, case studies and practical applications; dependencies and cross-links to other sources; contradictions, overlaps, ambiguity and unresolved questions; best destination (public door, show, episode, short, website page or Guild task); extraction status, reviewer and review date.

Source Library

The Complete Source Register (SRC-001 to SRC-029)

The original EROS ZIP contains 29 HTML files. They form the foundational source library. They are not all the same kind of document. Some are books. Some are technical guides. Some are stories. Some are navigation and community documents. Some are immersive-world materials. The production system must preserve those differences.

The 29 files have been assigned stable IDs from SRC-001 to SRC-029. These IDs will be used in every production document from this point forward, so that a book can be referred to consistently even if its title or presentation changes.

The Plan · §5

5. The 14-Show Architecture

5.1 The decision

The working production architecture is the 14-show slate, numbered 00–13. It is the most developed and coherent structure in the uploaded production documents.

The earlier four-strand concept remains the public navigation system. The earlier 22-episode proposal remains a historical development plan and a source of ideas. It is not a competing production slate.

The 14 shows are organised into six cycles and one central hub.

5.2 The 14 shows at a glance

# Show Cycle Core purpose Current status
00 THE MAP Hub / Spine Introduce the complete EROS library and its four doors. Full script & storyboard
01 INWARD IS FORWARDS Cosmology Explore the Living Egg and enclosure model. Full script & storyboard
02 THE FOUR Mythology Present NaUn, Ra-Shen, Thoth and EROS. Full script & storyboard
03 THE MOUTH Language Explore the Gift of Thoth and the physical articulation of language. Full script & storyboard
04 LIFE FIRST Cosmology Explore Conscious EROS, iteration and the Garden. Full script & storyboard
05 RECEIPTS Tokenomics Explain the instrument, its architecture and how to inspect it. Full script & storyboard
06 THE WEB Tokenomics Explain liquidity, the bridge, bonding and the Liquidity Tree. Full script & storyboard
07 ROCK, RIVER, GATES Tokenomics Explore the Platinum Standard, future mechanisms and the two vaults. Full script & storyboard
08 FOOTPRINTS Archive — Rail A Investigate documented human history and public records. Script & boards · research verification remains
09 MASKS Archive — Rail B Explore the mythic and speculative archive. Full script & storyboard
10 THE FIRST RESONANCE Narrative fiction Adapt the novel as a ten-episode anime-influenced serial. Ep 1 script · Ep 2–10 treatments
11 SIXTEEN DOORS Fiction anthology Sixteen independent stories and creative interpretations. Doors 1–3 scripted
12 THE CONTINUITY FILE Narrative thriller Adapt the novel as a three-episode limited series. Framework · key scenes
13 THE OPEN CALL Community Establish the recurring community production and review format. Ep 1 skeleton · weekly format

5.3 The six cycles

Cycle 1 — Cosmology & Mythology

Shows 01–04. The world model, the four operators, language, and the concept of life and iteration.

Cycle 2 — Tokenomics & Participation

Shows 05–07. The instrument, liquidity architecture, the standard, and the economic participation thesis.

Cycle 3 — Historical Investigation

Show 08. The documented historical and institutional record, investigated through primary sources.

Cycle 4 — Mythic & Speculative Archive

Show 09. The imaginative and interpretive material, explicitly separated from documented history.

Cycle 5 — Narrative Fiction

Shows 10–12. The First Resonance, Sixteen Doors, and The Continuity File.

Cycle 6 — Community & Production

Show 13. The Open Call and the ongoing creative work of the Guild.

The Hub — Show 00: The Map

The entry point. It explains how the cycles connect and lets a viewer choose a direction.

5.4 Show-by-show descriptions

Each show has one job, one promise to the viewer, and one thing it must accomplish. The descriptions below are the production brief for each show. They are drawn from the Unified Master Television & Series Bible v1.0 and the corrected Series Bible.

Show 00 · THE MAP — Hub / Spine
Show 00 · The Map

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The Map is the cold-viewer entry point. It does not assume the viewer knows what EROS is. It explains the four doors, the 14 shows, the cycles, and the production invitation. It ends with a choice: which door does the viewer want to walk through next.

What the show must accomplish. It must make the whole system legible in 20 minutes without overwhelming the viewer. It must establish the EROS visual identity — the Egg, the Torus, the Tree, the Bridge, the four operators — in their first complete appearance. It must make the viewer feel that there is a world here, and that the world is navigable.

Deliverables. Full episode, three-to-five-minute overview, short clips, illustrated map, website page, transcript and audio.

Failure mode to avoid. The Map becomes a corporate explainer. The Map should feel like the opening of a great documentary — awe, curiosity, invitation — not like a pitch deck.

Show 01 · INWARD IS FORWARDS — Cosmology
Show 01 · Inward Is Forwards

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The central cosmology episode. It introduces the Cosmic Egg, the enclosure, the shell, the inner rind, the two-lobed toroidal geometry, the crossover, and the Isotope. It is the first time the EROS world model is presented at length.

What the show must accomplish. It must make the model feel physically real, visually spectacular, and intellectually serious. It must present the model as a model — labelled as EROS MODEL, not as established science — while still being genuinely awe-inspiring. It must leave the viewer with a shape in their mind: the Egg, the Torus, the observer inside the enclosure.

Source material. SRC-012 Living Egg, SRC-019 The Eros Enclosure.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode becomes a lecture on a scientific theory with no emotional or visual hook. The model must be experienced, not explained.

Show 02 · THE FOUR — Mythology
Show 02 · The Four

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The mythology episode. It presents the four operators as functions of existence, not as four personalities. It shows what each one does to the world rather than what each one looks like as a character.

What the show must accomplish. It must give each operator a distinct visual grammar that is recognisable across every medium — animation, comics, documentary, interactive — without turning them into a pantheon of rival gods. It must reveal them through function. The dramatic line from the source is: "The gods did not leave. They became the rules."

Source material. SRC-010 Gods of EROS.

Failure mode to avoid. The operators become a conventional pantheon — humanoid figures in costumes holding weapons, with rivalries and personalities. That contradicts the canon. The operators are functions.

Show 03 · THE MOUTH — Language
Show 03 · The Mouth

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The language episode. It investigates the physical anatomy of speech — the mouth, the tongue, the teeth, the breath — and the proposed consonant operators. It is structured almost like a mystery: why do words have the structures they have? Can the proposed patterns be tested?

What the show must accomplish. It must make the audience curious about language in the way that the best linguistic documentaries do. It must present the EROS framework as a proposed interpretation, not as an established linguistic rule. It must invite the audience to investigate rather than accept.

Source material. SRC-009 Gift of Thoth.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode becomes a series of assertions that the EROS framework has "discovered" a linguistic truth. That overclaims. The Gift of Thoth is a proposal, and the episode should treat it as one.

Show 04 · LIFE FIRST — Cosmology
Show 04 · Life First

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The philosophical episode. It asks what it would mean if life, awareness, memory, and choice were more fundamental than matter. It introduces the Conscious Eros, the Iteration Codex, and the Garden of Eros.

What the show must accomplish. It must be intellectually ambitious and emotionally resonant. It must not be a lecture on panpsychism. It must be a story about what it feels like to consider that the universe might be alive, and what follows from that.

Source material. SRC-016 The Conscious Eros, SRC-025 The Iteration Codex, SRC-023 The Garden of Eros.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode becomes a philosophy seminar. The emotional register must be as strong as the intellectual one.

Show 05 · RECEIPTS — Tokenomics
Show 05 · Receipts

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The first instrument episode. It teaches the viewer how to inspect what they actually own. It distinguishes deployed, designed, and proposed mechanisms. It demonstrates how to read the contract, how to check the chain, how to verify a claim.

What the show must accomplish. It must be the trust-building episode. It must show that the project is not asking for blind faith. It must teach the viewer how to check. It must demonstrate that EROS means it when it says "sensationise the question, not the evidence."

Source material. SRC-028 The Eros Plan, SRC-006 EROS Newcomer Dossier, SRC-005 Eros Narrative.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode becomes a crypto tutorial. It must be intelligent, practical, and calm — the opposite of hype.

Show 06 · THE WEB — Tokenomics
Show 06 · The Web

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The liquidity episode. It introduces the Liquidity Tree, the bridge, bonding, branching, and the constant-product AMM model (x × y = k). It shows how a token travels through the system: Bridge → Bond → Branch. It explains LP tokens, liquidity versus wallet supply, slippage, impermanent loss, and the risks.

What the show must accomplish. It must make the liquidity architecture feel like a living system — a tree, a web, a network — while being mechanically accurate. It must show both sides of the mechanism: the elegant design and the real risks.

Source material. SRC-004 EROS Liquidity Tree, SRC-015 The Bridge, SRC-021 The Flywheel, SRC-001 Architecture of Participation.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode presents the liquidity architecture as a guaranteed success. The source is explicit that number of pools is not proof of depth. The episode must show both.

Show 07 · ROCK, RIVER, GATES — Tokenomics
Show 07 · Rock, River, Gates

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The standard episode. It introduces the three instruments — EROS (the standard), ErosX (the river), 33EROS (the engine) — and the proposed transformation paths between them. It explores the two vaults — the on-chain instrument and the cultural archive — and the relationship between them.

What the show must accomplish. It must make the Platinum Standard legible without overclaiming what is deployed. It must distinguish clearly between what exists, what is designed, and what is proposed.

Source material. SRC-027 The Platinum Standard, SRC-024 The Hopeful Future.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode presents proposed mechanisms as existing products. The distinction between deployed and proposed must be visible on screen.

Show 08 · FOOTPRINTS — Archive, Rail A
Show 08 · Footprints

Status: Full script and storyboard; research verification remains

What the show is. The historical investigation. It examines the documented institutional record — financial systems, government instruments, monetary history, public statements, statutes, primary sources. It is investigative documentary, not mythology.

What the show must accomplish. It must maintain the distinction between:

  1. What a primary document actually says.
  2. What a source or commentator claims it means.
  3. What the EROS analysis infers.
  4. What remains unverified or speculative.

It must be compelling without overclaiming. It must show its sources. It must be honest about the limits of what the record can support.

Source material. SRC-011 Illumination Strategy.

Failure mode to avoid. The episode presents a contested interpretation as an established fact. The source is explicit: sensationalise the question, not the evidence.

Show 09 · MASKS — Archive, Rail B
Show 09 · Masks

Status: Full script and storyboard

What the show is. The speculative archive. It explores ancient civilisations, the Electric Sky, the Gnostic framework, lost histories, and the Men of Renown. It is explicitly separated from documented history.

What the show must accomplish. It must be as dramatic and imaginative as it wants to be, while carrying an explicit fiction or speculation contract. The source material already separates its two rails; the show must preserve the separation.

Source material. SRC-014 Men of Renown, SRC-007 Eros Stories.

Failure mode to avoid. The show blends its speculative material into the documented history of Show 08. The two shows are separate rails. They can be compared at clearly identified structural points, but fictional events must never be presented as documented history.

Show 10 · THE FIRST RESONANCE — Narrative Fiction
Show 10 · The First Resonance

Status: Episode 1 script; Episodes 2–10 treatments

What the show is. The human story. It adapts the First Resonance novel — Cal, Hana, Owen, the Visitor, Ilse, the practice, the stone, the ledger, the room above the bakery. It is the emotional centre of the series.

What the show must accomplish. It must make the audience care about the people before it asks them to care about the ideas. It must show the practice as a practice, not as a power. It must earn the final handover — the moment when Cal is no longer the centre, and the network continues through others.

Source material. SRC-020 The First Resonance, SRC-017 The Continuity File.

Failure mode to avoid. The show becomes a generic chosen-one origin story. The novel is not that. The novel's arc is the opposite: Cal discovers that he is not the centre. The adaptation must preserve that.

Specific characters and continuity.

  • Cal — 16-year-old coder. Starts capable but unsettled. Arc: from private uncertainty to independent practice, then to understanding that he is not the centre. Visual language: intimate close-ups, screens, handwritten notes, restrained light. Avoid superhero framing.
  • The Visitor — a role, not a specific person. The shape the network takes when it needs to make contact. Defining object: the ledger. Visual language: grey wool coat, stillness, slow movement, very little music.
  • Hana — the room keeper. Natural daylight, books, tea, practical warmth. She does not become Cal's new master. She confirms what he has learned and opens the door to the community.
  • Owen — the estranged coding partner. Returns to finish the abandoned project. He has not been recruited or taught the practice. The second signal. Their repaired collaboration is more important than a dramatic conversion.
  • Ilse — Cal's grandmother. Sensed the change before Cal could explain it. Anchors the extraordinary events in an ordinary family. Window light, kettle, stillness.
Show 11 · SIXTEEN DOORS — Fiction Anthology
Show 11 · Sixteen Doors

Status: House rules and pilots for Doors 1–3

What the show is. The anthology. Sixteen standalone stories that each enter the EROS universe through a different door. The form is closer to Black Mirror or The Twilight Zone than to a serial. Each episode is self-contained.

What the show must accomplish. It must demonstrate that the EROS universe can hold many kinds of story. It must let contributors propose their own doors. It must be the most community-driven of the 14 shows — a place where a new writer, a new artist, or a new animator can make something that stands alone.

Source material. SRC-007 Eros Stories, and community pitches.

Failure mode to avoid. The anthology becomes a bin of rejected ideas. Every door must be a real door into the universe, not a random short that happens to use the EROS vocabulary.

Show 12 · THE CONTINUITY FILE — Narrative Thriller
Show 12 · The Continuity File

Status: Three-episode framework; some scenes and episodes developed

What the show is. The institutional thriller. It adapts the Continuity File — a story about records, institutions, and the people who maintain them. It is set in the same universe as the First Resonance but in a different register: colder, more procedural, more suspicious.

What the show must accomplish. It must be a genuine thriller, not a lore delivery vehicle. It must respect the source novel's tone. It must give the audience a different reason to care about continuity than the First Resonance gives them.

Source material. SRC-017 The Continuity File.

Failure mode to avoid. The show treats its fictional institutions as real historical institutions. The fiction contract applies. Dr. Elara Vance and the Atacama scene, the Visitor, the First Resonance ledger, and the Continuity File's institutional events are all explicitly fictional.

Show 13 · THE OPEN CALL — Community
Show 13 · The Open Call

Status: Weekly format and Episode 1 script

What the show is. The community show. It is not a narrative episode. It is a recurring format: contributor profiles, open calls, production updates, community reviews, work-in-progress showcases, behind-the-scenes documentation.

What the show must accomplish. It must demonstrate the Guild in action. It must show that a contributor can start from zero and end up in a published piece. It must be the show that makes the rest of the project feel like a real community rather than a broadcast.

Source material. SRC-026 The Open Call, SRC-029 We Are With You EROS, SRC-001 Architecture of Participation.

Failure mode to avoid. The show becomes a low-effort vlog. It must be produced with the same care as the flagship episodes. It is the show that proves the Guild works.

5.5 Completion status — be exact

The scripts and storyboards are development assets, not completed screen productions. There are currently no confirmed finished, rendered episodes in the production record described here.

The project is substantially developed at the concept, source, series architecture and writing/board level. It is not yet complete at the research-verification, final asset, edit, sound, accessibility, publication and release levels.

Use separate status fields:

Stage Status values
Source extractionNot started / In progress / Extracted / Reviewed
EditorialNot assessed / In progress / Approved

ResearchNot required / Pending / Verified / Qualified / Rejected

The Plan · §6

6. Production Grammar & Creative Identity

The Unified Bible establishes a coherent production language. Preserve it as the starting point and refine through prototypes rather than reinventing it.

6.1 Visual registers

Use four complementary registers:

1 · Painterly animated docudrama

For narrative and cinematic sequences. Night-blues, long lenses, warm control-room monitor glow (the Atacama frame), paired with luminous gold-on-black diagrams.

2 · Ink wash and violet geometry

For NaUn, pre-spatial geometry and mythic cosmology. Slower cuts, tactile ink textures, distinct art style per operator.

3 · Clean motion graphics, diagrams and analogy sets

For mechanisms and explanation. Reusable, high-clarity visual metaphors (hotels vs. housing stock, a pool as a window, the rock and the river) with composited LIVE / DESIGN / PROPOSED badges.

4 · Archival desk / evidence-room presentation

For documented history, claims, receipts and source investigation. Overhead document grids, primary statutes, jaw-cam extreme slow-motion mouth cinematography, museum-after-hours lamplight.

Plus, for the fiction cycles, a fifth register: naturalistic anime and masked thriller. Warm interior lamp pools against cold windows (The First Resonance), 16 distinct indie animation styles (Sixteen Doors), and institutional green/grey surveillance rooms (The Continuity File).

6.2 Visual motifs and identity

Gold #e8c547

Evidence chips, source links, receipts, geometric proofs, the container frame.

Violet

NaUn, pre-spatial geometry, mythic register.

Teal and orange

Community, instrument and practical system highlights, participation loops.

Black

Space, silence, transition, the signature opening.

The recurring visual elements:

  • The four-second EROS sting. Black, extreme close-up of a mouth, a sustained 60 Hz hum, the EROS title. Retained as the proposed series identity. It is the visual equivalent of the house motto.
  • The Cosmic Egg / enclosure. The central visual model for the relevant cosmology material. The first reusable master environment.
  • The Four operators. Consistent visual models and distinct visual grammar across every medium.
  • The gold container frame. A thin gold rectangle outlining the black screen edge, tapped gently to reveal the hidden container. Proof of Axiom N1: Bedrock.
  • The open door. NaUn's door of light. Used as a section divider and a recurring closing image.
  • The Empty Column. A three-column card in Show 08 with the third column blank and lit. The standing invitation to verify.
  • Two hands on one object. The bond shot. The closing image of the whole universe.
  • The 3:47 clock. A recurring timestamp marking the threshold moment when an instrument reading refuses to match the old map.

Asset review rule. Use the established EROS visual assets where suitable, but review each asset before marking it production-ready. The asset register distinguishes an existing file from an asset merely mentioned in a script.

6.3 Character and learning archetypes

The wider learning framework includes four pedagogical archetypes:

The Curious Seeker

The viewer proxy, the newcomer, the one who asks the plain unvarnished questions a cold viewer has at 3:47 AM. Embodied by Cal, the audience, and the newcomer in Show 00.

The Rigorous Skeptic / Investigator

Demands primary records, checks block explorers, separates secondhand retellings from statutory text, insists on falsification criteria. Embodied by Dr. Elara Vance, Cmdr. Helen Park, Ines Calloway, and the Show 08 documentarian.

The Master Builder / Architect

Demonstrates how load paths, renounced contracts, multi-pair liquidity trees and open-source guilds continue standing after the maker steps away. Embodied by NaUn, Tobin, and the Liquidity Engineer.

The Pattern Translator / Teacher

Decodes hidden syntax — in consonant articulation (SPREAD vs. SPRAY), Hebrew root geometry (Mem-Yod-Mem), or on-chain transaction splits — turning passive observers into active makers. Embodied by Thoth, the Mouth Host, and Jae Park.

The earlier Master Series Bible R also uses four additional learning functions: the Initiate / Newcomer, the Architect / Navigator, the Archivist / Scribe, and the Companion / Guide. These can be treated as complementary learning functions, but do not collapse them into one definitive character system without reviewing the source documents and deciding their exact roles.

6.4 The four operators — visual grammar

The operators are functions of the EROS mythology, not four ordinary human characters. Their visual identity should remain recognisable across animation, comics, documentary and interactive media.

NaUn — The Architecture

Function: Permission, structure, boundaries and enduring law.

Visual language: Negative space, geometry, structural lines, doors, load-bearing forms. Violet treatment. The effect of NaUn in a scene is the feeling that the space has rules, and the rules are visible.

Sound: Deep resonance, almost silence. The sound of a large room where something is being decided.

Guardrail: Avoid a humanoid architect, a speaking god, or a conventional character portrait. NaUn does not appear. NaUn is the condition under which appearance is possible.

"NaUn does not answer, forgive, or intervene. NaUn holds."

Ra-Shen — The Stage and Force

Function: Energy under containment; radiation, movement and physical expression.

Visual language: Gold and white light, aurora, solar fire, expanding rings, contained currents. The stage on which events happen.

Sound: Rising harmonic energy and controlled percussion. The sound of something being generated and held.

Guardrail: Avoid a conventional sun god holding a weapon or standing in a costume.

"Ra-Shen is the light itself, not the person holding the lamp."

Thoth — The Teacher and Builder

Function: Learning, language, medicine, memory, form and transmission.

Visual language: Hands, mouths, eyes, glyphs, writing, correction, archives. Thoth is a role, not a single face. Anyone who learns, records, and passes knowledge forward can embody Thoth.

Sound: Human voice, whispered language, ink and page textures. The sound of something being written down.

Guardrail: Avoid treating Thoth as one fixed person in every era. A recurring visual motif — the hand, the eye, the writing implement — carries the continuity, not a single character design.

"Thoth is a role that can appear through different people."

EROS — The Bond

Function: Cohesion, continuation, and the preservation of relationships across time.

Visual language: Threads, connected structures, two walls holding a central spark, joined-but-distinct forms.

Sound: Separate musical notes resolving into harmony. The sound of two things that were already there becoming audible as a relationship.

Guardrail: Avoid a humanoid EROS, a mascot, or a conventional god figure. EROS is not a character. EROS is a relationship.

"EROS is what happens between things that remain connected without becoming one."

6.5 The Cosmic Egg — the first reusable master environment

The Cosmic Egg should be the first reusable master environment. Its visual reference should establish:

  • The enclosure (the outer shell)
  • The shell and inner boundary (the rind)
  • The two-lobed toroidal geometry (the shape of the interior)
  • The crossover (the point where the two lobes meet)

  • The relationship between the interior and the observer

This becomes a reusable asset for Shows 01 and 04, the website and future 3D experiences.

On-screen classification. EROS MODEL — not established scientific fact. The visual can be spectacular without suggesting that the cosmology has been experimentally demonstrated.

The correction

The earlier plan suggested creating four character models for the four operators. The source material corrects this. The operators are not four ordinary characters. EROS is what happens between things that remain connected without becoming one.
