  • 5.1 A boy of eight on a roof at dusk, tracing the horizon with a finger. The horizon looks slightly too near.
  • 5.2 The same boy at twelve, same roof, a notebook now, a ruler, the horizon marked in pencil.
  • 5.3 At fifteen, the same roof, a telescope. The marks have moved.
  • 5.4 At eighteen, the roof at dawn. The boy and a friend, side by side. The friend asks, "What are you looking at?" The boy says, "Whether it still works."
  • 5.5 Final image: two hands on a single telescope. Bond.
Part 6 · The Invitation

The Invitation

This is the section that answers the only question that matters: what can I do?

You do not have to wait for a central team to finish a show. You can take a source, a concept, a character, a visual, or a task and begin developing something in parallel, while keeping the relationship to the larger EROS project clear. That is the central community invitation of the project. It is what makes the Guild a production network rather than a fan club.

We create. We expect the community to parallel work with us or fractally branch off from our inspiration.

Five Contribution Pathways

There are several pathways a parallel contributor can take. The pathways are not mutually exclusive. You can start with a single task, move to a personal project, form a studio cell, and eventually produce a branch. The system is designed to let contribution grow.

PATHWAY 1

The Single Task

Pick up a Guild brief, complete it, submit it, see it published. The smallest unit of contribution. You do not need to understand the whole universe to make one thing that belongs in it.

1–4 HOURS

PATHWAY 2

The Personal Project

Take on a larger piece of work — a comic, an audio episode, a visual novel chapter — and produce it under the Guild structure. One person, one larger deliverable, the same brief format and the same review process.

1–4 WEEKS

PATHWAY 3

The Studio Cell

Form a small group to produce a larger work together. Two to five people. Shared brief, shared credit, shared deadline. A cell can grow, split, or dissolve as its members choose. It does not need central permission to form. It needs to register, adopt the brief format, and agree to the canon tiers.

1–3 MONTHS

PATHWAY 4

The Experimental Branch

Produce work that deliberately diverges from the canon, and publish it as a Tier 4 branch. Labelled clearly. Allowed to exist openly. The universe grows by division, not by central expansion. Every branch that passes the Bond Test strengthens the whole.

VARIABLE

PATHWAY 5

The Research Contribution

Verify sources, build evidence registers, check claims. Research is a contribution pathway equal to production. The Atlas 8F correction in Show 08 is proof that a single verification pass can turn an overclaim into the strongest scene in the episode. Research is not a supporting role. It is the role that keeps the whole project credible.

1–8 HOURS PER CLAIM

The Four-Tier Canon

Parallel work does not automatically become canon. It is classified by tier. The tiers are not a hierarchy of quality. They are a hierarchy of authority. A Tier 4 work can be better than a Tier 2 work and still not be part of the canon.

Tier 1 · Core Source Canon

The 29 foundational source files and verified technical records. Locked. Immutable reference floor. The canon. The thing everything else is downstream of.

Tier 2 · Verified Expansion

Scripts, diagrams, adaptations and production material checked against Tier 1. A parallel studio cell's work can be Tier 2 if it is checked against the source and approved.

Tier 3 · Community Variation

Independent creative work that honours the core framework but may have its own artistic interpretation. It can be Tier 3 if it is a creative interpretation that honours the framework and passes the Bond Test.

Tier 4 · Experimental Branch

Alternative, divergent, or deliberately speculative work. Allowed to exist openly as a labelled alternative, never silently merged into the canon.

The fractal test. If you make a door, does the door contain the universe? If you make a scene, does the scene contain the practice? If you make a diagram, does the diagram contain the mechanism? If the answer is yes, the branch is sound. If the answer is no, the branch is decoration.

The Contribution Brief

Every task brief must contain twelve fields. This is the smallest practical production unit. A contributor should be able to open a brief and know exactly what to make, in what format, and to what standard, without needing to read the rest of the project documentation.

EXAMPLE BRIEF

TASK-0009 · Design the Cosmic Egg master reference

Show / episode / source: Show 01 · Inward Is Forwards · SRC-012 Living Egg, SRC-019 The Eros Enclosure

Studio: Visual Design

Why it matters: The Cosmic Egg is the first reusable master environment. It becomes the visual grammar for Shows 01 and 04, the website, and future 3D experiences. Without it, no cosmology episode can be produced.

Exact deliverable: One 4K still, multi-angle (3 views minimum), showing the outer shell, the inner rind, the two-lobed toroidal geometry, the crossover, and the Isotope.

Constraints: MODEL only. Do not render as established scientific fact. Gold #e8c547 linework on black. Violet where the geometry demands. No photorealistic surfaces.

Acceptance criteria: A stranger can identify the shell, the lobes, the crossover, and the Isotope without labels. The visual holds up at 4K and at 400px. It reads as a vessel, not a planet.

Format / spec: PNG or EXR, 4K, 16:9 and 1:1 versions.

Reviewer: The Visual Studio lead and the Show 01 director.

Credit: Named in the visual inventory, the asset register, and the episode credits.

These are the kind of tasks that can be picked up by a contributor on day one. Each is bounded, completable, and meaningful enough to matter. The first ten are the starter kit for the Guild task board.

No contributor should need to build an entire show to make a meaningful contribution. The smallest contribution should be small enough to be completed, and meaningful enough to matter.

The Empty Column

The Atlas 8F source-pass finding handed the production an original device that the rest of the slate can use. Whenever an episode touches a primary record, a three-column card appears. The third column is always blank and always lit.

What the document says Staging Camera No. 3, facing aft, booster jettison window, 10 seconds. Objects behind booster. Origin or identification could not be determined. DOCUMENTED
What the retelling says An object paced the re-entry vehicle for ninety seconds and phased out. SECONDHAND
What you find This column is yours.

The narrator ends every such beat on the third column: "This column is yours." It turns every verification gap into an invitation, which is what a participation loop needs, and it means no episode ever claims more than the record supports.

The Footprint Hunt is the standing weekly community event built on top of it. You find a primary document that bears on any claim in any show, fill in the empty column, and post it. The best find becomes the cold open of the next Open Call. It rewards exactly the behaviour the library says it values, and it creates a reason to come back every week.

What You Get

Credit

Every contributor is named. Every task has a credit line. Every branch has an author. The work is not anonymous.

Reusable assets

You can reuse the assets you and others have made. The asset register is open. The visual library is shared.

A path to more

A single task can lead to a personal project. A personal project can lead to a studio cell. A studio cell can lead to a branch.

Ownership that means something

The work is real. The credit is real. The contribution is visible. You can point at something and say "I made that."

A share in the growth

Every finished piece increases demand for EROS and TitanX. Every burn increases scarcity. The community that builds the universe shares in its success.

A universe you helped make

The value stays because the community built it. The universe is not extracted from you. It is made by you.

"The books provide the material. The series provides the narrative structure. The media platforms provide reach. The website provides continuity. The Guild provides the means to create. And the community gives the project its living expression."

We are not asking the community to invent EROS from scratch. We are giving them an organised world to interpret, explain, illustrate, test, and build upon.

The first task is not to produce everything.

It is to make the first complete example of the system — and then make it easy for others to repeat.

ONE LIBRARY. MANY DOORS. ONE GUILD.

Inward is forwards.

If you do not own it, you're not in it.

The invitation, one more time.

Find a piece of the EROS world that interests you. Check the source. Decide your tier. Pick up a task, propose a project, form a cell, or produce a branch. Every pathway is legitimate. Every contributor is named. Every piece of work that passes the Bond Test strengthens the whole.

The Footprint Hunt is open. The task board is open. The Empty Column is yours.

Build with us, or fractally branch off from our inspiration. The universe grows by division, not by central expansion.

EROS Series Bible · Part 1

Shows, scripts and storyboards built from the 29-file EROS library (EROS_Library_LOCAL.zip)

Prepared for Peter · November 2026

0. How to read this

This document turns the library into a television slate. Section 1 is the slate, one show per cluster of books. Section 2 is the full 20-minute script and storyboard for the cosmology and mythology show, the one you asked for next. Section 3 holds the Eros Plan overview and the three merged tokenomics shows, each with timed beats and boards. Section 4 holds the rest of the slate, a book-by-book map of all 29 files, and ideas on presentation format with a recommendation.

Three production rules I applied. Change any of them and the scripts bend easily.

  • Twenty minutes means about 2,300 spoken words. The rest is picture, music and silence. Every script below is written to that budget.
  • Every claim wears a chip on screen. OBSERVED (a measurement anyone can check), MODEL (an axiom the books state and label), STORY (dramatised or mythic), HYPOTHESIS (soft, labelled, not settled physics). The books already do this with Layer 1/2/3 tags and Law 11, "label speculation." On screen it lets the show be as sensational as you like without ever being caught out. The Enclosure book's own objections section is the template: a cosmology that names its weakest points is not a sales pitch.
  • Tokenomics shows carry a LIVE or PROPOSED badge on every mechanism. The contract, the 5% flow fee split, the fixed supply and the pools are live and checkable. ErosX, 33EROS and the transform are a design discussion, not deployed. The badge is accuracy, not a disclaimer, and it keeps the shows consistent with the Platinum Standard.

House style across all shows: crypto first, story second, extraction never. Gold (#e8c547) is the chip and link colour. Violet is NaUn and the myth sequences. Teal and orange belong to the community shows. Every episode opens on the same four-second sting: a close-up of a mouth, a hum, the title card EROS. That is the Plan's own opening shot, and it becomes the series signature.

Fourteen shows across six cycles, one hub. Corpus, Media Index and the three 3D Universe pages are not shows. They are the menu and the end cards.

2. SHOW 01 · INWARD IS FORWARDS

Runtime 20:00. Format hybrid drama and explainer. Narrator warm, a little mischievous, never shouting. Frame character Dr. Elara Vance, the astronomer from the Living Egg prologue, dramatised and chipped STORY.

Look. Three visual registers, so the viewer always knows what kind of statement they are watching.

  1. The Atacama frame. Painterly night-blue, long lenses, a control room lit by monitors. Elara lives here.
  2. The explainer. Luminous diagrams on black, gold linework, one idea per shot.
  3. The myth. Ink wash and violet geometry, slower cuts, no text on screen except the operator names.

Music. One low sustained tone at 60 Hz under the whole episode that resolves into the closing hum. Strings only in the myth sequence.

Runtime map.

COLD OPEN · 0:00–1:30 · THE CRACK IN THE LENS

BOARDS

  • 1.1 Black. A single sound: wind. Slow push over the Atacama at night, the dish arrays small against a vast sky. Super: Atacama Desert, Chile. 3:47 AM.
  • 1.2 Interior control room, wide. One woman, Elara, alone, coffee gone cold. Monitors wash her face blue. Insert: a clock, 3:47.
  • 1.3 Close on the screen: a lensing plot, arcs of distant quasars bent around a galaxy. A line of the equation glows gold: the dark matter term.
  • 1.4 Elara's hand over the keyboard. She hesitates. Holds.
  • 1.5 Extreme close: the delete key. Press.
  • 1.6 The gold term dissolves. The rest of the equation stays. The arcs on screen do not change.
  • 1.7 Her face. She does not breathe.

NARRATOR (V.O.)

"3:47 in the morning. The Atacama desert. A woman has been staring at the same numbers for eleven hours. The data is clean. The calibrations are perfect. And it makes no sense."

ELARA (quiet, to the empty room)

"Twenty-five years I've added eighty-five percent invisible mass to this equation. I've never seen it. Nobody has."

(She deletes the term. The math still works.)

"What if the math is right... and the geometry is wrong?"

CHIP STORY · dramatised from the Living Egg.

SMASH CUT to the sting.

STING AND TITLE · 1:30–2:00

  • S.1 Pure black. A mouth in extreme close-up, no context. Lips part.
  • S.2 A hum. The 60 Hz tone from the score, now a voice. The screen's edge ripples with it.
  • S.3 Title card on the last of the sound: EROS. Four seconds. Under it, smaller: INWARD IS FORWARDS.

ACT 1 · 2:00–5:00 · THE LID

BOARDS

  • 2.1 The narrator's world: black void, one gold line draws a telescope's light path to a lens.
  • 2.2 Split screen: a real sky photograph on the left, the same photograph on the right with the horizon line highlighted. The highlight pulses.
  • 2.3 Diagram: a ratio, drawn as two numbers on a seesaw. Label: PARALLAX. It cycles through REDSHIFT, LENSING ARC. Every label is the same shape: a ratio.
  • 2.4 The sky as a lid. Camera pulls back from a standing figure to reveal she is on the inside curve of a bowl; the sky is the underside of a gold shell. The geometry flips smoothly.
  • 2.5 Sunrise on the inside of the shell. Light loops, orange and swollen. The figure squints and smiles.
  • 2.6 A board game, top-down, the board's edge in warm light. Pieces move. Then the same game on a board with no edges, the pieces drifting off. Silence.

NARRATOR

"Let's get one thing out of the way. Your telescope is not lying. Light arrives with the exact angles and wavelengths recorded. Nobody disputes that.

"What is in dispute is subtler. What does that light tell you about the shape of the space it travelled through? And here is the secret: nobody has ever measured shape directly. Every parallax, every redshift, every lensing arc is a measurement of a ratio. The ratio is real. The interpretation of the ratio is a choice."

CHIP OBSERVED (the ratios) · MODEL (the reading).

"So try this. Read the sky not as a far wall but as a lid. Read the ground under your feet not as a floor but as the skin of a curved bowl you are standing inside. That horizon, always slightly too near, always slightly too curved? That is exactly what a horizon would look like from inside a finite shell.

"Does the sunrise still land? It does. The moon still rises swollen and orange. All of it still works. That is the point. This asks you to give up nothing you have seen. It asks what all of it could also mean."

(Board 2.6)

"This is not a cage. Every game has a board, and the board is what makes play possible. The outward picture taught us that the board has no edges, and so no meaning. The Egg gives the edges back. Small means you cannot reach the edges. Inside means the edges are what hold you."

CHIP MODEL · Axiom E1: Enclosure.

ACT 2 · 5:00–7:30 · ZERO APPLES

BOARDS

  • 3.1 A table. One apple. The narrator's hand lifts it away. Zero apples.
  • 3.2 The table, the room, the walls dissolve in slow motion. Now zero everything.
  • 3.3 But a thin gold rectangle stays: the frame of the picture itself. Camera finds it, taps it. Label: the container you smuggled in.
  • 3.4 Two doors on a black stage. Left door: CREATED FROM NOTHING. Right door: ETERNAL. Both swing open onto the same blank. The narrator shrugs.
  • 3.5 Elara's monitors, now showing a single gold line drawing itself outward: structure first.

NARRATOR

"Picture zero apples. Easy. Now picture zero everything. No space. No time. No field. No potential. Try it honestly. The moment you picture it, you have smuggled in a container to hold the picture. And the container cannot be zero.

"That is not a trick. It is the floor. Absolute nothing cannot obtain. Something is always already structured. Every creation story that begins from a pure void asks the void to do work, and the void cannot pay.

"And the other story, 'it was always here'? Always existed is just another way of saying no reason. Two impossible stories, both unfalsifiable. Neither is a measurement. Both are commitments dressed as cosmology.

"The third option is to stop asking what came before the structure, and ask what the structure is doing."

CHIP MODEL · Axiom N1: Bedrock.

ACT 3 · 7:30–10:00 · THE COUNT, THE WEIGHT, THE FUNNEL

BOARDS

  • 4.1 A clock face. Its hands unscrew and fall away. What remains: tick marks, a counter ticking up. The counter becomes a heartbeat, a calendar page flipping, a tree ring, a staking lock counting down.
  • 4.2 Process words appear and burn into gold: BEGIN. CONTINUE. COMPLETE.
  • 4.3 Two balloons, side by side on black, both inflating at the same steady rate. When they touch the bigger one nudges the smaller. Arrows: weight is what this nudge feels like.
  • 4.4 A figure standing on a ground that rises to meet her feet, the ground drawn as a soft expanding arc. Caption: The ground is rising as much as you are falling.
  • 4.5 A flat timeline, past to future. The camera lifts it off the page and it bends into a funnel, a whirlwind seen from above. Different heights glow gold.
  • 4.6 The figure standing at one height inside the whirlwind, looking up and down the funnel.

NARRATOR

"Time. We were taught it is a fabric that mass can bend. Try the simpler reading: time is a count. One moment, then the next. One iteration, then another. Look at the words we use for anything that takes time. Begin. Continue. Complete. Every process word is a bounded count of iterations. A calendar is iterations counted. A heartbeat is iterations counted. Where nothing iterates, nothing passes.

"Weight. In one lineage called Expansion Theory, every atom grows at the same shared rate. Two bodies meet, and the larger one accelerates the smaller. Weight is the inertia you feel resisting that. The ground is rising as much as you are falling. No invisible rope across the void. Just two expansions, meeting.

"And now the strangest picture in the book. A whirlwind does not have a current moment. The base is not its past. The top is not its future. The whole structure exists at once. What if time is shaped like that? What if we are not moving through time, but standing at a height within it?"

CHIP MODEL · Axiom T1: Iteration · Expansion Theory is a minority lineage · the funnel is HYPOTHESIS.

ACT 4 · 10:00–13:30 · THE FOUR

Register shift: ink wash and violet geometry. Strings in. No chips here except STORY, held in the lower corner for the whole sequence.

BOARDS

  • 5.1 Black that has not yet decided what black is. Violet lines unfurl without touching, angles that are not yet space.
  • 5.2 NaUn: not a figure but an absence with a shape. A silhouette made of the gaps between lines.
  • 5.3 A first mirror, perfect. Then a hairline flaw. The flaw glints gold. A path opens through it.
  • 5.4 Ra-Shen: a sun drawn as a ring of radiating strokes, a stage lighting up beneath it. Outward energy meets a boundary and becomes an event.
  • 5.5 Thoth: hands, not a face. Letters fall like rain from a pair of hands, each one a mouth-shape. A child catches one and speaks.
  • 5.6 EROS: two walls and a spark between them. Mem, Yod, Mem. The spark holds the walls apart and together. Water beads on the glass.
  • 5.7 Four glyphs arranged as one shape. Not a pantheon: a grid.
  • 5.8 NaUn turning, walking away through a door built of light, not looking back. The door stays open.

NARRATOR

"Every culture told this part as a story. Here it is as a grammar.

"Before the Sun had a name there was black that had not yet decided what black was. Violet geometry unfurling in the void. Silence before tone. Then NaUn.

"NaUn did not push a single star. NaUn established the conditions under which a star could burn. The first act of creation was not making a thing. It was making a world in which things could be made.

"In the first mirror, a flaw. Not a mistake to erase. The flaw is the feature that lets learning begin. A perfect mirror shows only itself. An imperfect one opens a path.

"Then Ra-Shen, the sun that makes the stage. Outward energy, under boundary. Without it, possibility never becomes an event.

"Then Thoth, the teacher and the builder. Thoth does not hand down finished words. Thoth lends letters, and leaves the words to the made. The gift is the code. The stories are yours.

"And the fourth: EROS. The bond. Not a god you petition. The reason a lesson survives its first speaker. In Hebrew, the word for water is Mem, Yod, Mem. Two walls around a spark. Bond is not fusion. Bond is what holds two things in relation without collapsing them into one.

"Four operators. No fifth. Not a pantheon. A grammar. Egyptian and Greek names are masks the operators wore. The function is what the masks were pointing at.

"And here is the line that makes the whole mythology turn."

NaUn (V.O., low, unhurried)

"I will withdraw my face and see what they become."

NARRATOR

"Withdrawal is not absence. It is the final test of the architecture. If the system only runs while the Architect watches, it is unfinished. If it runs when the face is hidden, the rules were real."

(Board 5.8. The door stays open.)

ON-SCREEN, brief, after the sequence: the Hebrew letters and the sun, the speed of light and E = mc². Narrator, lightly: "The book notes that the sun's name, its fuel, its speed and its energy equation share four characters. Design or coincidence? The book says that is not its claim. Watch the pattern. Make your own call."

CHIP STORY · the number pattern is PATTERN, not proof.

ACT 5 · 13:30–15:30 · WHO LIVES HERE

BOARDS

  • 6.1 1950. A lunch table, a napkin, a man in shirtsleeves leaning in. Super: Enrico Fermi. Over lunch. Hand on napkin: Where is everybody?
  • 6.2 The same question redrawn on the shell: two dots, "here" and "there," labelled as layers of one body, folding together.
  • 6.3 Camera descends into the shell's depth, a cavity, an abdomen seen through a hand lens.
  • 6.4 Aurora over a mountain range, then rock art of serpents, wheels and ladders. A dissolve between them: the shapes match.
  • 6.5 A white blood cell near a wound, then a drifting luminous plasma form near a mountain, cut in rhythm.
  • 6.6 A cell, looking up, unable to see the body it lives in.

NARRATOR

"1950. A lunch in New Mexico. Enrico Fermi asks the question that has haunted astronomers ever since: where is everybody?

"Inside a finite shell, 'everywhere' stops meaning far away. 'Here' and 'there' are layers of the same body. The paradox does not get answered. It dissolves. What is left is not silence. It is depth. Looking across it with a radio telescope is like looking across your own abdomen with a hand lens.

"And space may not be empty. It conducts. Ancient peoples drew the aurora as serpents, wheels and ladders. What if some of the traffic in the sky is not visitors? What if it is physiology? Repair. Regulation. Immune response. A body does not have to be understood by its cells. It only has to keep them alive."

CHIP HYPOTHESIS · Electric Universe and plasma cosmology traditions · labelled, not settled physics.

ACT 6 · 15:30–17:30 · WHY THE MAP FACES OUTWARD

BOARDS

  • 7.1 Timeline across the screen: 1543, 1687, 1915. Each year a portrait silhouette, not a likeness.
  • 7.2 A page of relativity equations. A highlight sweeps it: does not require an infinite universe. Permits a finite one.
  • 7.3 Cold-war era telescopes, rocket gantries, satellite tracking stations. Money flows as a thin gold line from a ministry building to a lab.
  • 7.4 A card appears: THE STRONGEST OBJECTION. Text: "Dark matter is required by the data."
  • 7.5 Two columns. Left: what the model concedes. Right: what would break it. Items light up one at a time.

NARRATOR

"Fair question. If this reading is so tidy, why isn't it the map? 1543, Copernicus moves the Earth. 1687, Newton settles the framework. 1915, Einstein repairs it with curvature. And here is the quiet fact: relativity does not require an infinite universe. It permits a finite one. The shape question could have been reopened in 1915. It was not.

"Between the wars and through the Cold War, cosmology professionalised. The people who paid for telescopes, satellites and physics departments needed ballistic missiles, communications and navigation. The outward mathematics tracked satellites beautifully. This is not a conspiracy. It is an economic fact.

"Now the strongest objection. Mainstream physics carries dark matter because the exterior geometry demands it. The model does not deny the observations. It asks whether a different geometry would make the same observations intelligible without the placeholder. That is a legitimate question even if the answer turns out to be no.

"And here is what would break it. Persistent failure of any independent evidence for a second domain. Steady success of outside-view models that never need an interior. Or a decisive demonstration that light and matter behave in ways only the exterior map can hold. The book welcomes those tests. A cosmology that cannot name its weakest points is not a cosmology. It is a sales pitch."

CHIP OBJECTION · FALSIFIER.

ACT 7 · 17:30–19:30 · THE END OF THE MAP

BOARDS

  • 8.1 A montage of old maps being folded and a new one unrolling. No faces.
  • 8.2 A suburban kitchen at dawn. Someone says a word aloud: "begin." Close on the mouth. The word breaks into its sounds, each a small gold glyph.
  • 8.3 Three small cards: 5 MIN, THE MORNING DECODE. 2 MIN, THE MIDDAY CHECK. 3 MIN, THE EVENING NOTE.
  • 8.4 Atacama, dawn. Elara in the doorway of the control room, the sky going from violet to gold.
  • 8.5 Her screen: she names a new file, geometry, and saves it.

NARRATOR

"This is not the end of the world. It is the end of the map. Every so often a civilisation changes its picture of what is real. It happens three or four times in recorded history. The people who live through it call it chaos. The people who come after call it normal.

"You do not have to believe a word of what you have seen. The book offers three small practices instead. In the morning, say one word aloud and notice what your mouth actually did. At midday, check one belief against what you can actually test. In the evening, write one line about what iterated today. Ten minutes in all. No ritual. No leader.

"Because a model is only worth what it lets you do. The question is never whether the sky is a lid. The question is whether a new reading helps you see something the old one could not."

ELARA (V.O., at the screen)

"Inward is forwards."

TAG · 19:30–20:00 · SAME LAW, ANOTHER SCALE

BOARDS

  • 9.1 The Egg, spinning slowly. A thread of gold light peels from it and becomes a network of pools on a dark map.
  • 9.2 End card: the library door, the Corpus page, the Telegram link.

NARRATOR

"In the Egg, this law is called affinity. In a community it is called cohesion. On a chain it is called a bond. If you want to see the receipts, the next stop is Episode Five."

END CARD Corpus · NotebookLM public studio · Telegram t.me/Eros_Revival · Next: THE FOUR

Production notes for Show 01

  • Count the words. The narration above runs close to the 2,300 budget. If your edit runs long, cut the Fermi lunch (Act 5) before cutting the objection (Act 6). The objection is what makes the show trustworthy.
  • Casting. Elara is the only recurring human. One voice actress, or a stylised animated character with no photoreal face. She never speaks to camera.
  • Chips are a design element, not subtitles. Gold outline, small caps, bottom-left. They appear for three seconds on first use and stay faint for the rest of the scene.
  • Reuse. The mouth sting, the gold container frame, and the violet myth style become the visual grammar for the whole Cosmology Cycle.
  • Deliverables. Master 16:9 at 20:00. Cutdowns: Act 1 as a 3-minute short ("The Lid"), Act 2 as a 90-second short ("Zero Apples"), Act 4 as a 4-minute short ("The Four"). These feed the Three Shorts slots each book already has.
3. THE PLAN AND THE TOKENOMICS SHOWS

The Eros Plan is the spine, four volumes: I The Instrument, II The Demand, III The Cosmology, IV The Production. Show 00 walks all four in twenty minutes. Shows 05, 06 and 07 then take the instrument and the demand apart in depth, merging the Dossier, Narrative, Bridge, Flywheel, Liquidity Tree, Architecture of Participation, Front Door and Platinum Standard into three episodes. The same four-second sting opens each one.

For these shows the on-screen badge system is LIVE (checkable on a block explorer now), DESIGN (an arrangement of live pieces, no new contract), and PROPOSED (not deployed). That is how the shows carry the technical limits without ever sounding like a disclaimer.

SHOW 00 · THE MAP · the Plan overview

Runtime 20:00. Format an animated isometric map of a city. The library is the city, each volume is a district, and the camera flies between them. One narrator, plus the newcomer as a silent point-of-view character. Core line "Crypto first. Story second. Extraction never."

Job of the episode. A newcomer stumbles in from Telegram or X and should think: this is interesting, clear, entertaining, gamified. It has to explain the whole plan without compressing it into a pitch.

COLD OPEN · 0:00–1:00

NARRATOR "Nobody hands you a shield when you walk into crypto. They hand you a chart. They hand you a promise. Nobody sits down and tells you what to watch out for. So here is a map instead."

DISTRICT I · THE INSTRUMENT · 1:30–4:00

  • B.1 Camera drops into a quiet block of the city: a vault with a glass door and the sign THE RECEIPT.
  • B.2 A contract address draws itself in gold. Four labelled arrows leave one transfer: burn, staking, lock, liquidity.
  • B.3 A block explorer hovers over the city. The camera zooms in on a field, owner(), and the answer.
  • B.4 Super over a standing coin: LIVE.

NARRATOR "Before the story, the token. Before the film, the key. EROS is a fixed-supply token on PulseChain. The contract has no administrator who can rewrite the rules. Every transfer splits four ways. All of it is checkable by anyone, at any hour, without asking anyone's permission. The instrument is not a promise. It is a receipt. The deeper detail lives in Show 05."

DISTRICT II · THE DEMAND · 4:00–7:30

  • C.1 A flywheel on a hill. Four spokes: Production, Attention, Stake, Participation. A hand gives it a push.
  • C.2 The equation arrives on a clean wall: Attention + Narrative + Work = Sustained participation. Beneath it, three tickers fade out one by one: loud, quiet, gone.
  • C.3 Ten thousand wallets as a field of dark windows. One lights. Then ten. Then all of them.
  • C.4 A web of pairs, a hundred and thirty-three glowing nodes, edges thickening as pools connect.
  • C.5 The lock: a price chart on one side, a library on the other, and a key between them.

NARRATOR "Supply without attention dies. Attention without work leaves. Community without activity disappears. That is not a slogan. It is the autopsy report of most tickers that launched loud and went quiet. The flywheel is the answer. Production and story bring attention. Attention brings people in. The token and the web give them a stake. Participation funds more production. And the army may already be here. Ten thousand TitanX holders who forgot they were given a uniform. The price can open the door. Purpose is what makes someone stay."

DISTRICT III · THE COSMOLOGY · 7:30–11:30

  • D.1 The map folds and becomes the Egg, turning slowly. A hatch of shell opens.
  • D.2 Three quick vignettes at three-times speed: the sky as a lid (Show 01), four glyphs forming a grid (Show 02), a mouth speaking one word (Show 03).
  • D.3 Corridor of doors, each one a book: Living Egg, Gods of Eros, Conscious Eros, Gift of Thoth.

NARRATOR "Here the map turns strange, and the strangeness is the point. The cosmology says we live inside something, not floating in an empty room. The mythology names four operators, not a pantheon: the architect, the stage, the teacher and the bond. The language says the mouth is the first instrument you ever played. None of this is asked of you as belief. Every layer is labelled. And every layer says the same thing in a different dialect: bond is what survives."

DISTRICT IV · THE PRODUCTION · 11:30–15:00

  • E.1 An open warehouse with sixteen doors, each marked with a role: writer, artist, coder, composer, translator.
  • E.2 A machine at a long table reading submissions from every desk. It does not write. It lays two contradicting pages side by side and a speech bubble reads: do these resolve, or does one want to be a heresy?
  • E.3 A four-second film: a mouth, a hum, the title. Caption: this shot can be made this weekend.
  • E.4 Three stacked layers, not a ladder: EDUCATION, MEDIA, WORLD. A figure steps between them freely.

NARRATOR "This is where a book stops being a book. The Plan names sixteen roles and a creation model. There is an engine, but it is not the author. It is a combiner and a consistency-checker, the editor who never sleeps and never plays favourites. Its best work is naming a contradiction and handing it back to the guild. The stages are layers, not a ladder. Education. Media. World. Anyone can start a Stage Two asset at their own scale. The book is not asking you to be George Lucas. It is asking you to make the four-second shot. Then the next one."

THE SCOREBOARD · 15:00–17:30

  • F.1 Three plinths in a row, each with a small light: ATH BREAK, 333 POOLS, MEDIA PHASE.
  • F.2 Each plinth lights and unlocks the next district. Under the second: PROPOSED.
  • F.3 A card: Falsification criteria. The Plan lists what would prove it wrong.

NARRATOR "Three public milestones. A stable break above the previous high triggers the rebrand and the revival campaign. Reaching 333 qualifying pools is the design threshold for the next instrument, ErosX, and the deeper game between the two. The media production phase comes after that. These are stated goals, not forecasts. And the Plan prints the conditions under which it would be wrong, because trust is the product."

PIN THE DOOR · 17:30–19:30

  • G.2 The newcomer walks to a sign and pins the folded map to it.

If you make things, Volume IV is a guild with no permission required. Short path: this show, the Dossier, and the Narrative. Every other book is a door."

SHOW 05 · RECEIPTS · tokenomics, part one

Runtime 20:00. Format documentary with a hard-boiled edge. Sources Newcomer Dossier, Eros Narrative, The Bridge (instrument, risk register), Plan Volume I, Front Door. Theme the instrument as ownership and architecture, not a chart.

Time Beat
0:00–1:30 Cold open · The founders who walked
1:30–2:00 Sting
2:00–5:30 The Confession · what to check before you touch anything
5:30–9:30 One transfer, four destinations

COLD OPEN

  • R.1 A conference room, empty chairs, a ticker on the wall still scrolling. A figure carrying a box of fees walks out through the back door.
  • R.2 A community chat, the messages slowing, then still.
  • R.3 One chair is still occupied. Light on the face of someone staying.

NARRATOR "You have watched them leave. Not the coins. The people who made them. One by one the founders took their fees, their inflation, their exit, and they walked. The tickers are still there. Nobody is home. This is the story of one that is different, and why."

THE CONFESSION · 2:00–5:30

  • R.4 A checklist on a wooden table. Items stamp in one at a time: VERIFY THE CONTRACT. USE THE OFFICIAL BRIDGE ONLY. KNOW YOUR SLIPPAGE.
  • R.5 Two nearly identical token cards. One is real, one is a copy. The viewer has three seconds to pick.
  • R.6 The bridge: bridge.pulsechain.com in gold. Other bridges greyed.

NARRATOR "Check before you touch anything. Fake tokens copy real names, and a wrong address spoils everything built on it. Use the official bridge only. And one detail that trips up almost every new buyer: the transfer fee plus typical price impact lands near six percent. Leave the exchange's default slippage and the swap simply reverts. Set it once and the trade completes."

ONE TRANSFER, FOUR DESTINATIONS · 5:30–9:30

  • R.7 A single coin, hovering. It splits four ways in slow motion: toward a burn address, toward a staking pool, toward a lock, toward a liquidity pair. Each destination labelled.
  • R.8 The supply meter: 333,333,333,333. The burn address ticks only upward.
  • R.9 Super: LIVE. Twenty-eight months of on-chain life.

NARRATOR "Fixed supply, 333 billion, set at birth. Every transfer splits four ways: part is removed from circulation for good, part rewards stakers, part locks staked tokens for a time, and part deepens the liquidity pair. The design carries its strength and its consequence together. It operates without a discretionary admin, and that cuts both ways. No one can rewrite the rules, and no one can rescue a mistake."

OWNERSHIP · 9:30–13:00

  • R.10 A set of keys on a table. A hand slides them across, and they fall through a grate into water.
  • R.11 owner() queried on screen. The result is an empty address.
  • R.12 A founder-shaped coin crumbles when the founder walks out. A network-shaped coin keeps growing.

NARRATOR "Renounced does not mean abandoned. It means the lever is gone. A coin built around a founder expires when the founder leaves. A network compounds. The people who stayed when there was nothing to extract are the signal, not the noise. Survival itself is the story. That is what the Front Door letter says, and it is why the letter is addressed to the one person who did not walk away."

THE RISK REGISTER AS A FEATURE · 13:00–17:00

  • R.13 A gallery wall of framed cards: THIN POOLS. FAKE ADDRESSES. SLIPPAGE. BRIDGE ERRORS. IMPERMANENT LOSS.
  • R.14 A thin pool with a small trade: a big wobble. A deep pool with the same trade: a ripple.
  • R.15 An LP exit: the viewer gets back the pool's current mix, not what they put in.

NARRATOR "Most projects hide the risk register. This one prints it. Thin pools move on small flow, in both directions. An LP exit returns the pool's current mix, not necessarily what you deposited. Fees need volume, and no manual can invent volume. It can only refuse magical thinking."

THREE QUESTIONS · 17:00–19:30

  • R.16 Three doors. Q1: Who can change the rules? Q2: Where is the supply? Q3: Who stays when nothing is pumping?

NARRATOR "Three questions you can ask of anything. Who can change the rules? Where is the supply? Who stays when nothing is pumping? Ask them of everything. Then see what is left."

Sources The Bridge (Poolonomics, Pulseonomics), EROS Liquidity Tree, Architecture of Participation, Front Door, The Flywheel (pools), Plan Volume II. Theme human behaviour: why a network of pairs beats one giant pool.

Time Beat

COLD OPEN

  • W.1 A hotel lobby. Guests check in and out. Tagline: spot trades are hotel nights.
  • W.2 Pan to a neighbourhood: rows of houses, lights on. Multi-pair depth is housing stock.
  • W.3 An exit sign. One hotel empties in a minute. The neighbourhood does not.

NARRATOR "Spot trades are hotel nights. Deep, multi-pair liquidity is housing stock. A district. Harder to empty in one exit. That one picture is most of this episode."

A POOL IS A WINDOW · 2:00–5:00

  • W.4 A glass window onto a city. Inside, only a fraction of the buildings are visible. Caption: Pool depth is not total demand or total supply.
  • W.5 Seesaw diagram of x × y = k with a coin dropped in. In a shallow pool the seesaw swings wide. In a deep pool it barely tilts.
  • W.6 Two viewers at one window. One owns the asset. One provides the pool. Same view, different stakes.

NARRATOR "A pool is a window, not the whole city. In a shallow pool a small trade moves the price a lot. In a deep one it barely moves. And your perspective depends on what you own. If you own the asset, depth is your exit. If you provide the pool, depth is your infrastructure. Pool count alone does not tell you how deep the market is. The book says so. We say so."

POOLONOMICS · 5:00–8:30

  • W.7 Two machines. Machine A: deposit two tokens, a third inflationary reward spits out and gets sold into the market. Machine B: two tokens you chose, trading fees return more of the underlying.
  • W.8 A hand-drawn LP token, a receipt with a share written on it.

NARRATOR "A classic farm pays you in a third-party reward token that often gets sold straight back into the market. Bonding is the contrast. You pair two assets you actually want, you own the LP receipt, and you earn a share of trading when there is trading. You are not watching a candle. You are a market-maker. And you name your doorway, promote it, make it an identity."

THE TREE · 8:30–12:00

  • W.9 A seedling. Three moves: bridge, bond, branch. A bridge span, a handshake, a branch.
  • W.10 Ten coin icons on the ground. Each pairs with EROS and sprouts a base pool. Then the pools pair with each other, level by level, up to one Final Root LP.
  • W.11 A counter: Ten coins. Nineteen pools. One root. 2N−1.
  • W.12 Super: DESIGN. Every piece already exists. We only arrange them. The optional vault appears faintly, labelled PROPOSED.

NARRATOR "Bridge. Bond. Branch. Three moves, and that is the whole thing. Bring the tokens across the official bridge. Pair each with EROS, equal value both sides, and keep the LP receipt, an ordinary token. Pair the receipts with each other, level by level, up to one root. Ten coins make nineteen pools. The tree is an arrangement of pieces that already run. It adds no contract. The mathematics builds the tracks. Human psychology is the train."

THE TEN THOUSAND · 12:00–15:30

  • W.13 The dark windows again, now with a letter slipped under each door.
  • W.14 A figure at a desk reading. Super: Jake Sharpe built TitanX. He knows who was here.
  • W.15 Eight steps of a bridge lighting in order. Caption: the four-step sequence in the letter. (Pull the exact four steps from The Front Door when you cut this.)

NARRATOR "The simplest, highest-leverage action is not creating another token or making enormous promises. It is reminding ten thousand holders what they already hold. The bear market took away the noise. It also gave time to build without anyone watching. The question is what happens when people start watching again."

THE LOOP THAT CAN FAIL · 15:30–18:30

  • W.16 A four-frame loop: someone posts a live pair address and a reason to care. Holders answer and refuse fake admins. Someone adds size to the pool they promote. A trade hits it and fees accrue.
  • W.17 At each frame a red marker blinks: can fail here.

NARRATOR "Attention. Community. Liquidity. One loop. It can fail at any step. The manual cannot invent volume. It can only show you the shape of the loop and what you can do at each frame."

TAG The web from above. 133 nodes glowing, 200 more dark. The next number is 333. Next: ROCK, RIVER, GATES.

Runtime 20:00. Format myth-meets-engineering: a river valley as the central set. Sources The Platinum Standard, The Hopeful Future, The Flywheel (two vaults, price-to-purpose lock), Plan Volume II (strategic stack). Theme a standard, a game, and a reason.

COLD OPEN

  • K.1 A gold mine at dusk. The price on a board rises. The machines roar. More gold comes out of the ground.
  • K.2 The mine floods the market. The price board falls.
  • K.3 A single rock in a stream. The water goes around it.

NARRATOR "If the price of gold rises, people mine more gold. The supply expands. EROS has a fixed original supply, and a burn address that only grows. That is the difference between a metal and a standard."

THE ROCK · 2:00–5:30

  • K.4 A great stone in a river valley, gold veins in it. Label: EROS. LIVE.
  • K.5 Rule of three: a store of value, a transfer currency, a reward currency. Three different jobs. A single token tries all three and a pile of incentives collides.

NARRATOR "A monetary system does not need one token to do every job. A store of value, a transfer currency and a reward currency have different requirements. EROS is the foundation: scarce, slow, the thing you measure against. You do not spend the rock every day."

THE RIVER · 5:30–9:30

  • K.6 Water flowing past the rock. Two tributaries labelled ErosX and 33EROS. Both PROPOSED.
  • K.7 A triangle forms between three tokens, three pairs, three edges. Small arbitrage bots like otters moving along the edges, closing gaps.
  • K.8 Each rotation: a small fire, a small deepening of the pool, a small burn.

NARRATOR "The river carries movement: ErosX for spending and transfers, 33EROS as a second path. Two paths, one engine. Burn, bond, deepen. When both are live the ecosystem becomes a triangle. Rotation across any edge feeds the burn and lets equivalence bots close the gaps. To be clear, this part is a design discussion, not a deployed product. The code is written. It does not deploy on a date."

THE GATES · 9:30–12:30

  • K.9 Three gates across the river. A gate is a panel of real instruments: MARKET DEPTH. POOL COUNT. VERIFIED CODE.
  • K.10 A calendar page tries to push a gate open. The gate does not move. A gauge reaches its mark and the gate swings open on its own.

NARRATOR "Earned, not scheduled. The transform waits on three things: market depth, pool count and verified code. Not a date. A calendar cannot open these gates. Only the conditions can."

BUILD ON THE ROCK · 12:30–15:30

  • K.11 A world map. Pins drop: London, a Chinese New Year market, a Tokyo street. Each pin pulls a new river from the rock.
  • K.12 Four shapes in order: deposit EROS, burn most of it, buy-and-burn the new coin, deepen the pool.

NARRATOR "The pattern is open. A community takes its own idea, say LondonX or BeastX, and uses the transform as its launchpad. Every node has its own identity and its own audience. Every node shares the same rock. The rock does not dilute. It deepens."

THE STACK AND THE TWO VAULTS · 15:30–18:30

  • K.13 Five horizontal bands in a cross-section of the valley: pDAI, Atropa, Dysnomia, EROS, PulseChain, and the bridge as a bridge. Each band tagged LIVE, DESIGN or PROPOSED.
  • K.14 Two vaults side by side. One is steel and code. The other is a library. A light passes between them.
  • K.15 The lock: a chart and a library joined by a key.

NARRATOR "The Hopeful Future describes a five-layer stack, each layer naming its own confidence and its own gates. And two vaults, on-chain permanence and cultural permanence. One is code and control. The other is meaning and continuity. If people arrive only for a rising chart, they may leave when it turns red. If they find a universe they value, they have reasons to stay through the quiet seasons. The lock is the connection between the market cycle and the cultural cycle."

TAG The rock in the stream. Super: EROS is the standard. The river is the game. The world is the reason. Next: FOOTPRINTS.

4. THE REST OF THE SLATE

Treatments with beat structure for every other show. Each one is ready to be expanded into the same script-and-board format as Shows 01 and 05–07 in a second pass.

SHOW 02 · THE FOUR · Gods of Eros

Hook Every mythology wants something from you: a side, a prayer, a lineage. This one wants nothing. Format the myth register of Show 01 stretched to twenty minutes, one art style per operator. NaUn is violet geometry and negative space. Ra-Shen is burning gold stroke. Thoth is hand-inked glyphs. EROS is water and thread.

Beats

  1. The First Silence. Black that has not yet decided what black is. NaUn establishes a possibility, not a thing.
  2. NaUn · The Permission. Two creators: one adjusts every stone by hand, one builds a structure that remembers. The second is greater, not because the ego is smaller but because the work is finished.
  3. Ra-Shen · The Stage. The Abundance Law and the Balance, the two directions of outward burn under boundary.
  4. Thoth · The Teacher. The House of Light, the First Correction, the Lending of Letters, the Tree in the Middle, the Deep Ledger. One sequence per idea, each under ninety seconds.
  5. EROS · The Bond. The Oldest Law: the ray does not end, it changes address. The Two Sons, one bond.
  6. The Breaking. One tongue, one code, a tablet that shatters. Every language a splinter that still carries the grain.
  7. The Four Laws, tested. Each law is shown broken, in one shot: the machine that stops when the architect does, the stage with no energy, the learner who never learns a name, the generation that starts from zero.
  8. The Architect's Quiet. NaUn walks through the door they built and does not turn around. Not failure. The work held.

Chips STORY throughout. PATTERN on any number-and-letter observation. Note Show 01 Act 4 is the four-minute trailer for this episode.

SHOW 03 · THE MOUTH · Gift of Thoth

Hook SPREAD lands. SPRAY continues. The difference is one consonant, and you can feel it in your jaw before anyone explains it. Format half lab, half game show. The audience is invited to say words aloud. A "jaw-cam" (extreme close-ups of mouths in slow motion) is the signature shot.

Beats

  1. The question. You have said these words your whole life. Have you ever looked inside one?
  2. Consonants as operators. Position is syntax. Words are compressed programs. Each consonant is a physical act with one invariant identity.
  3. SPREAD vs SPRAY. The demonstration the whole episode hangs on.
  4. The candidate pairs. ADVISE vs ADVICE and other pairs, shown live, with the audience as the test. (This beat lines up with your candidate-pairs list for the book.)
  5. Two doors, one insight. The book describes a mathematician at the Wolfram Physics Project reaching a parallel insight from the AI side. Show both doors and let them meet.
  6. Build a shared tongue. Two strangers argue past each other, then name the shapes of their words and stop arguing.

Chips HYPOTHESIS and TEST IT YOURSELF. The mouth is the court. Anything that cannot be tested with your own mouth is chipped PATTERN.

SHOW 04 · LIFE FIRST · Conscious Eros, Iteration Codex, Garden of Eros

Hook Matter is what a frozen decision looks like from outside. Format one explanation told four times at four levels, the structure the Codex itself uses: the 18-year-old, the undergraduate, the graduate, the doctoral. Each level is five minutes. Same demonstrations, deeper each pass.

Beats

  1. The bedrock. Two things that cannot be false. Life is awareness, memory and choice. Matter is an effect of life.
  2. Four postulates and the freeze. When two postulates conflict, they freeze. Mass is the residue of unresolved conflict.
  3. The Water Principle. Freeze a kilogram. Weigh it. It is still a kilogram. Why ice floats, and what a practitioner can learn from it. A kitchen demonstration anchors the whole episode.
  4. The Five Forms. The Anchor-Drop, the Phase-Glide, the Crystal Expansion, the Compact and the Stutter-Step. Five silhouettes, five rhythms, one beat each.
  5. The practice. Two lines a night. Twelve chairs, no leader. Four months, four thresholds.

Chips MODEL. Every claim is tagged at its layer, as the Conscious Eros reference section already does.

SHOW 08 · FOOTPRINTS · Illumination Strategy

Hook Read the instrument, identify the decision, follow the resources, then ask what remained. Format investigative documentary in the archival-paper style. A desk, a statute, a contract, a budget line, a facility. No talking heads.

Beats

  1. The method. A press conference records what an administration wants understood. A statute records what the system is equipped to do. They are different evidence.
  2. The Ledger. Start with the Gold Reserve Act of 1934 and follow the revaluation.
  3. 1962 and the Tagalongs. The method demonstrated on a second case.
  4. The Architecture. The OAP Program.
  5. The Bond. How the footprints connect.
  6. The Last Card. The Footprint Files, one by one.

Chips DOCUMENTED, INFERRED, SPECULATIVE, matching the book's Layer 1, 2 and 3 tags. Caution this is the one show where a source pass comes first: every document on screen must be one the viewer can pull up. The Continuity File (Show 12) is the fiction companion and stays separate, the way the library keeps Rail A and Rail B apart.

SHOW 09 · MASKS · Men of Renown

Hook Two confusions, one Egg. A breakaway civilisation misread as gods. The enclosure's own life misread as visitors. Format a museum after hours: footprints as exhibits, with a docent narrator. The fiction contract appears on screen in the first ninety seconds so every viewer knows this is Archive 7, labelled as such.

Beats The quieter door between the two loud ones, the residual powers stored as giants and watchers, the god-masks, the enclosure's biologics misread as craft, and how to read residue without needing a throne. Chips ARCHIVE and STORY. It never competes with Illumination for evidence.

SHOW 10 · THE FIRST RESONANCE · serial

Hook A visitor keeps a ledger: 422 names of people he has taught, and eleven who are still walking. Format an anime-style serial. Book One, The Ray, runs ten episodes from the novel's ten chapters: a sixteen-year-old coder is tuned by a ray of light, taught face to face, and becomes the first conscious node of a practice meant to make the teacher unnecessary. Book Two, The Curriculum, is Season Two. Episode 1 is The Number He Did Not Type.

Series rule The protagonist's arc is to become unnecessary. Build every episode toward that.

SHOW 11 · SIXTEEN DOORS · Eros Stories anthology

Hook Arguments are forgettable. Stories are not. Format sixteen shorts of eight to twelve minutes, each in a different animation style. Spine pieces: The Gods Come Out of Hiding, The Living Egg, The Inside Door. Doors: From the Membrane, The Boy Who Watched the Sky Change, Under the Ice, Other Man, Nervous System, Tripling Up. Witness pieces: Shell & Spark, The Waters Again, The Flood That Never Ended, The Egg's Voice, The Unbroken Bond, The Choir at the Ridge, The Density.

Why this is the best fit for the Guild An anthology is the one format a decentralised studio can make in parallel. Each door is a self-contained commission: one writer, one visual lead, one composer, one voice. No door depends on another.

SHOW 12 · THE CONTINUITY FILE · limited series

Hook Four boxes on a cover sheet: Government, Market, Machine, Other. None can contain the answer. Format a slow thriller in three episodes, one per book: The Feed (a face in a satellite feed, a wallet in a classified log, eleven minutes of silence), The Stick (the stick breaks, don't strip the nerve, the button, "I'm in the cast"), The Chair (the Living Egg, the chair in the room, the record is theirs). A Commander is handed a face, a wallet and a form that does not exist.

Look PulseChain colours, per the book's brief. This is the show where AI actors make the most sense, because the cast is masked by design.

SHOW 13 · THE OPEN CALL · weekly community format

Hook One camera. One white paper on screen. Two videos a week, for six months, starting with TitanX. Format eight to ten minute episodes. No hype and no sermon: read it, think, say what you find. Segments Paper of the Week, Door of the Week (a community-made short from Show 11), The Scoreboard (the pool count and where it stands), Ask the Studio (viewer questions answered from the NotebookLM sources).

6. PRESENTATION IDEAS

Picking a format is picking a trade-off between consistency, cost, emotional reach and how many people can contribute. Here is every option on the table, followed by my recommendation.

Format Best for Strength Trade-off
Narration over images (essay film) Footprints, Masks Cheapest, most flexible, authoritative tone Needs a strong narrator and strong stills
Motion-graphic explainer Tokenomics, Life First Clean, consistent, scales across many episodes Can feel cold without a character
Painterly animated docudrama Inward Is Forwards Emotional reach plus explanation Needs a locked character and style bible
Anime or cel-shaded serial The First Resonance, Sixteen Doors Lowest barrier for young audiences; fans can contribute fan art Long runtime; style drift is the main risk
Comic or webtoon Every show Storyboards become the comic with almost no extra work Static; needs motion for the flagship
AI actors and virtual host Continuity File, Open Call The masked cast makes it a natural fit Uncanny valley; keep them stylised and disclosed as synthetic
Podcast and NotebookLM overviews All, as the audio layer Already in your pipeline Not a replacement for picture
Interactive 3D Shows 00 and 01 You already have three 3D Universe pages Needs hotspots tied to each episode
Community-made anthology Sixteen Doors The one format a guild can build in parallel Needs a house style so it feels like one universe

Recommendation: layer by purpose.

  • Cosmology gets the painterly animated docudrama with Elara as the human thread, because it needs both wonder and explanation.
  • Myth gets ink and violet animation. Different art style per operator.
  • Tokenomics gets motion graphics with analogy sets (hotels and housing, the rock and the river). It is the most reusable template and the cheapest to produce at scale.
  • Archive shows get narration over images. The documents are the star.
  • Fiction gets anime-style animation for the serial and the anthology, and AI actors for the Continuity File.
  • Community show gets a stylised virtual host plus viewer-made clips.
  • Every show ships with a comic cut, a three-minute short, and an audio overview. One storyboard feeds all of them.

Library integration. Each book already has top, middle and bottom cinema slots. Fill them the same way for every book: a 60 to 90 second trailer at the top, a three to four minute cutdown in the middle, the full twenty-minute episode at the bottom. The cutdowns marked in Show 01's production notes are the template.

7. PRODUCTION NOTES AND LIMITS

These are the genuine technical limits, not caveats.

  • Shot length. Current AI video tools produce short clips, a few seconds each. A twenty-minute episode is a few hundred shots. Every board in this document is written as a single prompt unit, so the storyboard is the shot list.
  • Character drift. Faces and costumes drift between clips. Lock Elara and the narrator's avatar with a character sheet before generating anything. The myth sequences are safer because the figures are abstract.
  • Text in video. Generated text is unreliable. Every chip, contract address, equation and caption is composited in the editor, never generated.
  • Voice. Record the narrator once, as a scratch track, and cut an animatic from stills first. Cutting the script against a voice is where the 2,300-word budget actually gets tested.
  • NotebookLM. Feeding a script into NotebookLM as a source gives you a style-consistent rough cut and a mind map for free. It will not hold the three-register look, so treat it as a rough cut, not a master.

Suggested order. Show 01 first, since it carries the visual grammar. Show 00 second, since it is the newcomer's front door. Shows 05 to 07 together, because they share a template. Cosmology Cycle shows 02 to 04 next, then the Archive and Story cycles.

Decisions only you can make.

  1. Does Elara stay as the recurring human thread across the whole Cosmology Cycle?
  2. One narrator voice across all shows, or one per cycle?
  3. Which art style is the flagship: painterly or anime?
  4. Is the Continuity File shown as AI actors, animated, or both?
  5. Which three books get their trailers first?

Next pass. Full scripts and boards for Shows 02, 03, 04 and 08 to 13, then a per-book trailer script for the cinema slots.

SHOW 02 · THE FOUR · 20:00

Narrator low, unhurried, almost a storyteller by firelight. Look myth register only: ink wash, violet geometry, one art style per operator. No chips except STORY, held in the lower corner. Music strings and one human voice, no drums until the Breaking.

Time Scene
0:00–1:30 The First Silence
1:30–2:00 Sting
2:00–5:00 I · NaUn, the Architect
5:00–7:30 II · Ra-Shen, the Stage

THE FIRST SILENCE · 0:00–1:30

  • 1.1 Absolute black. No sound. A very slow breath.
  • 1.2 Faint violet lines unfurl without touching. Angles that are not yet space.
  • 1.3 A single tone enters. The lines hold their breath.

NARRATOR "Before there was light, there was the possibility of light. Before there was matter, there was the law that allowed matter to exist. Before there was life, there was the architecture in which life could learn. And before the first mind looked upon the universe, the universe already contained the instructions for being looked upon."

(Beat of silence.) "The greatest creator is not the one who remains in control forever. The greatest creator is the one who creates something capable of continuing without them."

STING (mouth, hum, title: THE FOUR).

I · NaUn, THE ARCHITECT · 2:00–5:00

  • 2.1 NaUn as a shape made only of the gaps between violet lines.
  • 2.2 Two builders side by side. The first stands in the centre of a hall, adjusting every stone by hand. The second stands outside, drawing load paths and joints on a slate.
  • 2.3 Both walk away. The first hall's stones forget their order and slump. The second building stands.
  • 2.4 A mirror, perfect, showing only itself. Then a hairline flaw. A path opens through the flaw.
  • 2.5 A gate in the shape of the letter N, glowing, closed.

NARRATOR "NaUn did not push a single star. NaUn established the conditions under which a star could burn. The first act of creation was not making a thing. It was making a world in which things could be made.

"Consider two creators. One stays at the centre of every room, adjusting every stone. The creation thrives only while the hand is present. The other builds a structure that remembers: load paths, joints, thresholds. When that architect walks away, the building still stands. The second is greater. Not because the ego is smaller. Because the work is finished.

"In the first mirror, there was a flaw. It was not a mistake to erase. It was the feature that would let learning begin. A perfect mirror shows only itself. An imperfect mirror opens a path."

II · Ra-SHEN, THE STAGE · 5:00–7:30

  • 3.1 Gold stroke on black: a ring of radiating lines that becomes a sun.
  • 3.2 Heat presses on cold. Where they meet, a small storm of colour: a stage lighting up.
  • 3.3 Vibration as visible rings spreading across a pond. The rings collide, interfere, bloom into a spiral. Movement to frequency to resonance to chemistry, each step a title card.
  • 3.4 A first complex molecule assembling, slow and tentative.

NARRATOR "Then came the outward surge. Energy flooded the permitted channels. Radiation found its rings. Heat pressed against cold. This is Ra-Shen, the sun that makes the stage. The stage did not ask permission to light. It lit.

"Movement becomes frequency. Frequency becomes resonance. Resonance becomes chemistry. Somewhere in that enormous unfolding, complexity crosses a threshold, and the first spark of a complex molecule appears. Without outward energy under boundary, there is no stage. Possibility never becomes event." [PULL: the Abundance Law and the Balance wording for the on-screen cards.]

On-screen aside: the Hebrew name of the sun, Shin-Mem-Shin, set beside the speed of light and E = mc². NARRATOR "The book notes that the sun's name, its fuel and its speed share four characters. Design or coincidence? The book says that is not its claim. Watch the pattern. Make your own call." CHIP PATTERN.

III · THOTH, THE TEACHER AND BUILDER · 7:30–11:00

  • 4.1 Hands, not a face. Letters fall from them like rain, each one a mouth-shape in gold ink.
  • 4.2 A child catches one and speaks. A word forms in the air and holds.
  • 4.3 A house built of light: walls that let light become a living thing. Inside, a tree.
  • 4.4 A deep ledger, pages turning by themselves, entries written in many hands.
  • 4.5 A single glyph held up to a reversed eye. The glyph flips and reads the same.

NARRATOR "Thoth is not only the teacher. Thoth is the builder of forms: biology, memory, language, the wall that lets light become a living house.

"And here is the gift that changes everything. Thoth does not hand down finished words. Thoth hands down letters, operators, and leaves the making of words to the made. The gift is the code, not the sentence. What mortals build from the letters is their responsibility and their art. That is why language can grow. That is why every guild, every film, every game can speak in its own dialect without leaving the architecture.

"The letters are Thoth's. The stories are yours."

IV · EROS, THE BOND · 11:00–13:30

  • 5.1 A candle's flame, then its heat on a wall, then a plant leaning toward it, then a child reading by it, then the same child grown, teaching another. A single thread of light runs through every frame.
  • 5.2 The Hebrew word for water, Mem-Yod-Mem, drawn in the air: two walls and a spark.
  • 5.3 The spark holds the walls apart and together. Take the spark away and the water becomes plain material.
  • 5.4 Two sons, Ra-Shen and Thoth, side by side, and a third thread running between them that is not a rival.

NARRATOR "Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed in form. That law is older than the name EROS. The bond does not invent conservation. The bond is how conservation becomes story. What was heat becomes chemistry. What was chemistry becomes memory. What was memory becomes inheritance. The ray does not end. The ray changes address.

"In Hebrew, the word for water is Mem, Yod, Mem. Two walls around a spark. Bond is not fusion. Bond is the Yod that holds two Mems in relation without collapsing them into one. Without it, water is not water. It is just unordered material.

"One son powers. One son forms and teaches. Between them runs a function that is not a third competing for the throne. It is the reason either of them matters tomorrow."

V · THE BREAKING · 13:30–15:30

  • 6.1 A great tablet, one tongue, one code, the gate and the mouth agreeing.
  • 6.2 A tower of one mouth rising. Symbols pile on symbols. The silence between words is crowded out.
  • 6.3 The tablet shatters. Drums enter for the first time. Pieces scatter across a map.
  • 6.4 Close on one shard: the grain of the old code still visible in the fracture. Then another shard, another, each carrying the same grain.

NARRATOR "When the tablet broke, the code did not die. It scattered. In the first telling there was one tongue: not one nation, but one code close enough to NaUn's architecture that the gate and the mouth agreed. Then came the Breaking. Not only as punishment. As consequence. Pride built towers of one mouth owning the whole code. Complexity piled symbols on symbols until the silence between words was forgotten. The understanding fell.

"What survived was not corruption. Every tongue that followed is a splinter still carrying the grain. Hebrew. Egyptian mask-language. Greek names. The four remain four. No fifth god. No merged name."

VI · THE FOUR LAWS, TESTED · 15:30–18:00

Each law is shown intact for two seconds, then broken in one shot.

  • 7.1 NaUn's Law: a machine runs beautifully while a figure watches. The figure leaves. The machine stops.
  • 7.2 Ra-Shen's Law: a darkened stage with no light. Actors in costume, motionless. Nothing happens.
  • 7.3 Thoth's Law: a glowing creature that burns bright and never learns its own name. It fades.
  • 7.4 EROS's Law: a generation of children each starting from the same blank page, no one teaching the next.

NARRATOR "Four laws. NaUn's: a creation that cannot continue without its maker is unfinished. Ra-Shen's: without outward energy under boundary, there is no stage. Thoth's: without learning, energy never becomes life, and without form, energy never becomes a house. EROS's: without bond, learning does not iterate, and without iteration, nothing endures. Break any one and you can watch the world fail in a single shot."

VII · THE ARCHITECT'S QUIET · 18:00–20:00

  • 8.1 The first builder's hall and the second's, side by side again. A crowd of strangers walks through the second one, laughing, living.
  • 8.2 NaUn at the open door, built of light. Hand on the frame.
  • 8.3 A parent teaching a child. A programmer releasing code. A composer releasing music. A teacher watching students become teachers. Four quick cuts, each a door.
  • 8.4 NaUn steps through and does not turn around.

NaUn (V.O.) "I will withdraw my face and see what they become."

NARRATOR "The greatest test of a system is not whether it can run while the architect watches. It is whether it can run when the architect has stopped watching. The architect builds the doorway. The teacher teaches those who enter. The community becomes the living organism. The pattern moves from person to person. See the final beat not as biography. As archetype. The architect walks through the door they built and does not turn around. Not because the work failed. Because the work held."

END CARD Gods of EROS · the Corpus · Next: THE MOUTH.

SHOW 03 · THE MOUTH · 20:00

Narrator a curious host, first-person, quick and playful. Look a bright, high-key studio. Extreme close-ups of mouths in slow motion, the jaw-cam, are the signature shot. Graphics are hand-drawn on glass. Music light percussion; each demonstration ends on a clean drop.

COLD OPEN · 0:00–1:30

  • 1.1 A dinner table. Two people argue. Their lips move, the words slow and thickening in the air as small glowing shapes.
  • 1.2 The shapes do not match. One is round, one is angular. Neither person can see them.
  • 1.3 The argument ends. Neither has won. Neither is wrong.

HOST "You have argued past someone your whole life. So has everyone you know. Not because either of you was wrong. Because the words were different shapes in each mouth, and neither of you knew the shapes had names. This is the show that names them."

STING (mouth, hum, title: THE MOUTH).

THE QUESTION INSIDE THE WORD · 2:00–5:00

  • 2.1 The host holds up a card with a word on it: a job title. Say it aloud.
  • 2.2 The camera pushes into the host's mouth as it forms the word. The tongue, the lips, the breath, slowed to a crawl.
  • 2.3 The standard answer on a chalkboard: sounds point to a thing; the sounds are arbitrary. The host crosses it out.

HOST "Take a word that means something to you. A job title. A name you argue about. A word you are quietly proud of. Say it aloud. What just happened? Most of us were taught one answer: you made sounds that point to a thing. The sounds are arbitrary. The thing is real. The word is a label. Move on.

"This show proposes a different question, not an answer yet. A question. What if the word contains more than the label?"

SPREAD vs SPRAY · 5:00–9:00

  • 3.1 Split screen: jaw-cam on SPREAD, jaw-cam on SPRAY, synced.
  • 3.2 SPREAD: the mouth closes hard on the final sound. A gold dot lands on a line and stops.
  • 3.3 SPRAY: the mouth opens and the sound keeps going. A gold line continues past the edge of the frame.
  • 3.4 Back to the host, a single raised finger. "One consonant."

HOST "Two words. Same first four sounds. SPREAD lands. SPRAY continues. The difference is one consonant, and you can feel it in your jaw before anyone explains it. Say them both. Feel where the first one stops. Feel where the second keeps going. That is not a theory. That is your own mouth, giving evidence."

CHIP TEST IT YOURSELF. The mouth is the court.

CONSONANTS AS OPERATORS · 9:00–12:30

  • 4.1 A chalk board turning into a keyboard. Each key is a consonant. Pressing a key produces a small physical act drawn as a diagram of the mouth.
  • 4.2 Words as compressed programs: a short word unpacks into a sequence of small acts. Position is syntax: the same letters in a different order, a different program.
  • 4.3 [PULL] the first three operators from the Gift of Thoth reference table, each shown as one mouth-diagram and one gold glyph. Use the book's own wording for what each does.

HOST "Beneath the surface language you were taught sits a second layer you have been running since you learned to speak. Consonants are operators. Words are compressed programs. Position is syntax. This is the claim. Here is how to test it, and here is where it might break."

CHIP HYPOTHESIS. Any claim that cannot be checked with your own mouth is chipped PATTERN.

THE CANDIDATE PAIRS, LIVE · 12:30–15:30

  • 5.1 A studio audience, six people, each with a card. A pair of words flashes up: ADVISE and ADVICE.
  • 5.2 Jaw-cam on each. The audience says them aloud and marks a card: which one lands, which one continues?
  • 5.3 The tally, in gold. Then the host asks one person to say why.
  • 5.4 [PULL] two more pairs from the book's candidate list.

HOST "Now you try. Advise. Advice. Same letters except one. Say them. Where does the sound stop? Where does it carry on? Did you hear it? Good. Now tell the person beside you. That is how a shared tongue starts: with someone else saying, I felt that too."

TWO DOORS, ONE INSIGHT · 15:30–18:00

  • 6.1 Two corridors on a dark stage, each ending in a door. Left door: from the mouth. Right door: from the machine.
  • 6.2 Each door opens onto the same room.

HOST "The book describes a mathematician at the Wolfram Physics Project arriving at a parallel insight from the AI side. Two doors. One room. We are not claiming they agree on everything. We are saying you can walk in from either side."

CHIP The Wolfram parallel is reported by the book. Verify before repeating it elsewhere.

THE SHARED TONGUE · 18:00–20:00

  • 7.1 The dinner table again. The two people who argued. This time one pauses and says, "When you say that word, what does your mouth do?"
  • 7.2 Each says the word slowly. The two glowing shapes finally face each other. They fit, or they do not, but now they can see.
  • 7.3 The host at the table, quietly.

HOST "You can read inside any word, name what you are actually doing instead of arguing about what you mean, and build a shared tongue with anyone who hears the same architecture. Tonight, say one word out loud. Notice what your mouth did. That is the whole practice. The fog of conversation starts to turn into structure."

SHOW 04 · LIFE FIRST · 20:00

Narrator patient, a teacher who respects you. Format one explanation told four times, at four levels. The structure is borrowed from the Iteration Codex's own Levels section. Each pass is five minutes. The same two demonstrations, a kitchen kilogram of water and a handful of stones, return each time and go a layer deeper.

Look a plain kitchen table, daylight, a scale, a glass, a bag of ice. The cosmology never appears as spectacle here. It appears as a table, a glass and a hand. Music one acoustic instrument, nothing else.

COLD OPEN · 0:00–1:30

  • 1.2 The glass goes into a freezer. Time-lapse. The glass comes out, solid.
  • 1.3 Back on the scale. One kilogram.

NARRATOR "Freeze a kilogram. Weigh it. It is still a kilogram. Nothing was lost. Nothing was added. Something changed state. Hold that thought. We are going to spend twenty minutes on it."

STING (mouth, hum, title: LIFE FIRST).

LEVEL 1 · THE 18-YEAR-OLD · 2:00–7:00

  • 2.1 The narrator at the table. Two cards: Matter first, life late. Life first, matter as effect.
  • 2.2 Two things that cannot be false, written on a chalk slate: mathematics is the only objective phenomenon; absolute nothing cannot obtain. [PULL: use the Conscious Eros wording for the two statements.]
  • 2.3 Life drawn as three small icons: awareness, memory, choice.
  • 2.4 The glass of water again. Ice floats. A hand pushes it down. It rises.

NARRATOR "You were taught that matter came first and life turned up late, an accident inside a very large room. This show reads it the other way, as a model, not a laboratory verdict. Life is not biology. It is the thing that can be aware, remember and choose. Everything else is an effect.

"At this level, keep it simple. Something that remembers, and chooses, comes first. The rest is what it leaves behind. Ice floats, and we will come back to why."

CHIP MODEL.

LEVEL 2 · THE UNDERGRADUATE · 7:00–12:00

  • 3.1 Four small cards slide onto the table: know, not-know, be known, not be known.
  • 3.2 Two cards from opposite pairs collide, hard. The table shivers and the two cards fuse into a small grey stone.
  • 3.3 The stone is placed on the scale. The display reads a weight that was zero a moment ago.
  • 3.4 Time and space redrawn as readings, not containers: a ruler that measures a count, a clock that counts transitions.

NARRATOR "Four postulates. Four decisions at the source about what is real, what must be, what must not be. When two of them conflict, they freeze. And here is the pivot: mass is the residue of unresolved conflict. A body with mass is a body with many unfinished iterations held short of resolution. Mass is not a property of dead stuff. It is the weight of something that has not resolved.

"Energy is the bookkeeping of transitions. Space and time are readings, not containers. The postulate layer sits above the effect layer, and the correction changes everything downstream."

CHIP MODEL · Axiom P1: Postulate prior.

LEVEL 3 · THE GRADUATE · 12:00–16:00

  • 4.1 The glass of water from above. The ice, drawn in cross-section: a lattice with air gaps.
  • 4.2 A graph appears: rate on one axis, state on the other, a body drawn as a dot moving through the plane.
  • 4.3 Five silhouettes walk across the table, one at a time. Each one is labelled with a name and a rhythm: The Anchor-Drop. The Phase-Glide. The Crystal Expansion. The Compact. The Stutter-Step.
  • 4.4 A beam of light enters the frame and bends at the glass. Caption: what a beam of light does.

NARRATOR "Rate and state say what a body does. Coherence says what it builds. Time is the count of iterations. Weight is the meeting of two expansions. A body changes state by changing its relationship to the shell, and there are five stable ways it does that." [PULL: one-line definition of each of the five forms from the Iteration Codex.]

"Notice what the ice does here. The mass stayed invariant. The structure varied. That is the Water Principle, and it is the lab bench for everything else in the book."

CHIP MODEL · the Water Principle is the book's own demonstration.

LEVEL 4 · THE DOCTORAL · 16:00–19:00
